nv-power-1.claim: Orin NX and Orin Nano modules have one 3-channel INA3221 at I2C 0x40. Channel 1, VDD_IN, measures total module power. This is the best candidate for orin_power_watts, but the dataset does not say which channel is read.

nv-power-1.quote: The Jetson Orin NX series and Jetson Orin Nano series modules have a 3-channel INA3221 power monitor at the 0x40 I2C address. ... Channel 1: VDD_IN | Total Module Power
nv-power-1.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-1.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-power-2.claim: INA3221 channel 2, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV, measures the combined CPU, GPU and CV (DLA, PVA) rail. The r36.x pages have a typo here ('CPU, CPU and CV'), which r39.2.1 corrects.
nv-power-2.relation: cpu_gpu_power_watts plausibly = INA3221 ch2 VDD_CPU_GPU_CV (inferred; heartbeat source undocumented)
nv-power-2.quote: Channel 2: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV | Total power consumed by CPU, GPU, and CV cores; that is, DLA and PVA.
nv-power-2.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r39.2.1 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-2.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-power-3.claim: Every Orin Nano power mode has 0 DLA cores, 0 PVA cores and no NVENC. On Orin Nano, the VDD_CPU_GPU_CV rail therefore effectively carries CPU and GPU only.
nv-power-3.relation: on Orin Nano: cpu_gpu_power_watts (if ch2) = CPU + GPU power only (no CV engines)
nv-power-3.quote: DLA cores | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 ... PVA cores | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 ... dce: 384 nvenc: n/a se: 307.2
nv-power-3.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-3.section: Supported Modes and Power Efficiency > NVP Model Clock Configuration (Jetson Orin Nano 8GB / 8GB Super)

nv-power-4.claim: INA3221 channel 3, VDD_SOC, is the SoC core rail. It feeds the memory subsystem and the video and imaging engines (nvdec, vi, vic, isp). It is not one of our nodes unless orin_power_watts or device_power_watts maps to it.
nv-power-4.relation: VDD_SOC (unobserved) carries memory-subsystem and NVDEC/VIC/ISP load; it is part of VDD_IN
nv-power-4.quote: Channel 3: VDD_SOC | Power consumed by SOC core which supplies to memory subsystem and various engines like nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp etc.
nv-power-4.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-4.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-power-5.claim: An NVIDIA moderator states that VDD_IN is total SOM (module) power and that VDD_CPU_GPU_CV and VDD_SOC are sub-blocks: VDD_SOC is the SoC core rail, not the whole SoC. The sub-rails are therefore contained in VDD_IN.
nv-power-5.relation: containment: cpu_gpu_power_watts -> orin_power_watts (valid only if orin_power_watts = VDD_IN and cpu_gpu_power_watts = VDD_CPU_GPU_CV)
nv-power-5.quote: Yes, VDD_IN is Total SOM power. ... The VDD_CPU_GPU_CV is a CPU, GPU, CV (ie DLA & PVA) combined power rail. ... Yes, it is not whole SOC power. It is a SOC’s core rail which supplies memory subsystem, engines like decoder, encoder, vi, vic, isp …etc.
nv-power-5.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums - Orin NX Power Data from JTOP (reply #7, NVIDIA moderator rkasirajan)

nv-power-6.claim: A second NVIDIA moderator states that VDD_IN is the total and the other channels are individual hardware blocks. This supports containment rather than addition.
nv-power-6.relation: containment: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV and VDD_SOC are parts of VDD_IN, not additive to it
nv-power-6.quote: VDD_IN is the total power consumption and others are individual hardware blocks.
nv-power-6.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums - Orin NX Power Data from JTOP (reply #5, NVIDIA moderator DaneLLL)

nv-power-7.claim: An NVIDIA moderator confirms specifically for Orin Nano and NX that VDD_IN is total module power.
nv-power-7.relation: orin_power_watts (if ch1) = total Orin Nano module power
nv-power-7.quote: VDD_IN is total module power on Orin-Nano/NX series which has been documented in L4T developer guide
nv-power-7.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums - Jetson orin nano Power GUI (reply #3, NVIDIA moderator kayccc)

nv-power-8.claim: In a user's Orin Nano Power GUI readings, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV plus VDD_SOC (about 5.2 W) is well below VDD_IN (8.1 W). The sub-rails are parts of VDD_IN, and VDD_IN also holds other module loads (DDR, IO, regulator losses). Weak evidence from a non-staff post about someone else's device.
nv-power-8.relation: cpu_gpu_power_watts < orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN); the remainder is other module load; supports containment, against summing the rails
nv-power-8.quote: VDD_IN: 8081 mW, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV: 3654 mW, VDD_SOC:1535 mW question: if I add these 3 (VDD_IN, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV, VDD_SOC) together, it’s about 13.270 mW, it’s close but not equal to my 15 W budget setting.
nv-power-8.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums - Jetson orin nano Power GUI (post #1, user hank.fang.usa)

nv-power-9.claim: For Xavier NX (a different but analogous module), an NVIDIA moderator says VDD_IN also includes DDR and interface rails beyond the CPU/GPU/CV and SOC channels. By analogy only, this suggests VDD_IN minus the sub-rails is not just losses.
nv-power-9.relation: orin_power_watts (VDD_IN) = cpu_gpu_power_watts + VDD_SOC + DDR/IO rails + losses (Xavier NX analogy; not Orin-specific)
nv-power-9.quote: VDD_IN is the total power of module. VDD_CPU_GPU is VDD_CPU_GPU_CV. CV includes DLA, PLA and etc. There are other parts like DDR and interface power rails are included in VDD_IN domain.
nv-power-9.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums - Interpretation of Jetson NX power rail (reply #3, NVIDIA moderator Trumany)

nv-power-10.claim: VDD_IN is defined as module power only. None of the three Orin Nano channels covers carrier-board loads such as the display, the LTE modem or the heater. Those loads can show up in the sign-input INA238 power but not in orin_power_watts. This depends on BusPas wiring, which is unconfirmed.
nv-power-10.relation: containment (conditional on BusPas wiring): orin_power_watts -> input_power_watts; modem/display/heater load affects input_power_watts but not orin_power_watts (inferred)
nv-power-10.quote: the average and instantaneous power limits has been set for the VDD_IN channel to ensure that the total module power does not exceed the Thermal Design Power (TDP) budget.
nv-power-10.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-10.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-power-11.claim: The INA3221 sysfs interface exposes rail voltage (mV) and rail current (mA), not power. Any power value from sysfs:ina3221 must be computed by the reader as V x I. Rail V and I are not nodes.
nv-power-11.relation: identity (inferred): orin_power_watts = INA3221 in<i>_input x curr<i>_input / 1e6, computed by the BusPas agent
nv-power-11.quote: curr<j>_input | Gets rail current in milliamperes. | in<i>_input | Gets rail voltage in millivolts.
nv-power-11.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-12.claim: Average and instantaneous power limits are set on VDD_IN. When module power exceeds them, hardware throttles GPU and CPU clocks. This control loop runs within seconds, so it creates a lag-0 cycle with workload -> power. Record it as a feedback note, not an edge.
nv-power-12.relation: control (feedback note): orin_power_watts above TDP limit -> HW clock throttling -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-12.quote: the average and instantaneous power limits has been set for the VDD_IN channel to ensure that the total module power does not exceed the Thermal Design Power (TDP) budget. When the module power consumption exceeds the configured power limit, the module will perform hardware-based clock throttling
nv-power-12.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-12.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-power-13.claim: Orin Nano VDD_IN limits are 15 W average / 20 W instantaneous on the 8GB module and 10 W / 15 W on the 4GB module. Both are 25 W with Super flash configurations. An approx. 4.5 V under-voltage event triggers the OC1 throttle.
nv-power-13.relation: bound: orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN) capped near 15 W (8GB) or 10 W (4GB) average by control
nv-power-13.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 8GB | 15W | VDD_IN Average Power: 15W | OC2 | ... | VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 20W | OC3 | ... | Under Voltage: approx. 4.5V | OC1 ... Jetson Orin Nano 4GB | 10W | VDD_IN Average Power: 10W | OC2 | ... | VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 15W | OC3
nv-power-13.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-13.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > TDP limits table

nv-power-14.claim: Orin has three OC event types (under-voltage, average overcurrent, instantaneous overcurrent), with per-event counters in sysfs. The ~4.5 V under-voltage threshold applies at module level, not to the 12 V / 56 V sign input. A direct edge from input_voltage_volts is not documented; one would exist only if the BusPas converter lets the module input sag.
nv-power-14.relation: none documented between input_voltage_volts and throttling; conditional control path: module-input under-voltage -> CPU/GPU throttle -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-14.quote: There are 3 types of OC events in the Orin series, which are Under Voltage, Average Overcurrent, and Instantaneous Overcurrent events respectively.
nv-power-14.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-15.claim: OC event counts can be read from the oc*_event_cnt sysfs nodes. These counters are not in the telemetry. If BusPas logged them, they would label throttling hours.
nv-power-15.relation: none (unobserved throttle-event counter; candidate context variable)
nv-power-15.quote: The following sysfs nodes can be used to learn the number of OC events occurred: $ grep "" /sys/class/hwmon/hwmon<x>/oc*_event_cnt
nv-power-15.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-16.claim: When system input voltage falls below a safe level, the system is throttled to avoid shutdown. Here 'system input' most likely means the module input; mapping it to input_voltage_volts is an inference.
nv-power-16.relation: control (conditional, inferred mapping): low input voltage -> throttling -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-16.quote: If system input voltage drops below a safe level, the nvpmodel GUI displays a desktop notification to warn you that the system is being throttled back to avoid a shutdown due to insufficient power.
nv-power-16.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-17.claim: Battery overcurrent, PMIC voltage drop or temperature spikes raise OC alarms, which trigger hardware clock throttling. The OS is not notified, so the throttling state is unobserved.
nv-power-17.relation: none (unobserved hardware-throttling state reduces CPU/GPU clocks)
nv-power-17.quote: The firmware refers to these events as OC alarms, and triggers clock hardware throttling to handle them. ... The host OS is not notified of these events, but you can detect the drop in clock rates by using a performance measuring tool that samples the CPU cycle counters.
nv-power-17.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-17.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Hardware Throttling

nv-power-18.claim: Evidence against a large hourly effect: NVIDIA describes hardware (OC) throttling events as rare and transient, so they should barely move hourly-mean power unless a device sits at its TDP limit.
nv-power-18.relation: against: HW throttling expected to have small effect on hourly means
nv-power-18.quote: Like software throttling, hardware throttling may reduce performance. Because the triggering events are rare and transient in nature, though, the user experience is minimally impacted.
nv-power-18.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-19.claim: Firmware caps CPU and GPU clocks at three throttle levels so that they cannot draw more current than their regulators can supply. CPU/GPU power is bounded by control.
nv-power-19.relation: control: hardware clock caps bound cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-19.quote: To manage peak current consumption, the firmware supports capping the CPU and GPU clocks at three levels (light, medium, and heavy), as described in the device tree bindings. Clock capping prevents the CPU and GPU from drawing more current than their voltage regulators can supply.
nv-power-19.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-19.section: Hardware Throttling > Throttle Points and Vector Configuration

nv-power-20.claim: DVFS ties frequency to voltage: higher clocks need higher voltages. This is the documented mechanism by which workload-driven clock changes change rail power.
nv-power-20.relation: physical/control basis: workload -> clock frequency -> rail voltage -> cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-20.quote: Because clock frequency is proportional to voltage, dynamic voltage scaling is closely related to frequency scaling. For example, higher clock frequencies require higher voltages and vice versa.
nv-power-20.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-21.claim: cpufreq scales CPU frequency with CPU load, and CPU thermal management can override it. Load drives power, and temperature feeds back on power.
nv-power-21.relation: control: CPU load -> CPU frequency -> cpu_gpu_power_watts; cpu_temp_celsius can cap it (feedback note, lag-0 cycle)
nv-power-21.quote: For example, cpufreq implements load-based scaling, which adjusts the CPU frequency according to how busy the CPU is. CPU thermal management, however, can override the target frequency of cpufreq.
nv-power-21.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-22.claim: The default CPU governor is schedutil (utilisation-driven, aimed at power saving), so by default CPU frequency and power follow load.
nv-power-22.relation: control: CPU utilisation -> CPU frequency -> cpu_gpu_power_watts (default configuration)
nv-power-22.quote: The default CPU frequency governor is schedutil. which is primarily aimed at power saving.
nv-power-22.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-22.section: Related Tools and Techniques > CPU Frequency Scaling

nv-power-23.claim: GPU 3D frequency scaling is on by default, so GPU load sets GPU clock and therefore GPU rail power. That DeepStream's load reaches the GPU is an inference this page does not mention.
nv-power-23.relation: control: GPU workload (e.g. deepstream_running, inferred) -> GPU frequency -> cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-23.quote: GPU 3D frequency scaling is enabled by default.
nv-power-23.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-23.section: Related Tools and Techniques > GPU 3D Frequency Scaling

nv-power-24.claim: The memory controller (EMC/MC) and DRAM have their own DVFS to save power, so memory traffic changes module power (VDD_SOC/DDR, inside VDD_IN).
nv-power-24.relation: control: memory traffic -> EMC/DRAM frequency and voltage -> VDD_SOC/DDR power -> orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN)
nv-power-24.quote: Additionally, BSP implements Dynamic Voltage and frequency scaling for the memory controller (EMC/MC) and DRAM to save power.
nv-power-24.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-25.claim: Evidence against a RAM-to-power edge: EMC frequency follows client bandwidth requests and measured bandwidth use (30% up / 20% down thresholds), not the amount of RAM allocated. RAM in use (mem_used_gb) has no documented path to power.
nv-power-25.relation: against: no documented mem_used_gb -> power edge; EMC scaling depends on bandwidth, not occupancy
nv-power-25.quote: If current memory bandwidth usage exceeds 30%, the BPMP will scale up the EMC frequency, and if the memory bandwidth usage is lower than 20%, the BPMP will scale down the EMC frequency.
nv-power-25.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-25.section: Memory Power Management > EMC Frequency Scaling Policy

nv-power-26.claim: The multimedia engines (NVDEC, NVENC, NVJPG, VIC; Orin Nano has no NVENC) scale their clocks with load. Video decode and scaling load therefore raises SoC-rail power. DeepStream using NVDEC/VIC is an inference.
nv-power-26.relation: control: video decode/VIC load (deepstream_running, inferred) -> engine frequency -> VDD_SOC -> orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN)
nv-power-26.quote: The reported load of each engine by the actmon will be used to complete load-based dynamic frequency scaling, which is implemented in the tegra_wmark devfreq governor.
nv-power-26.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-26.section: Related Tools and Techniques > Multimedia Engine Frequency Scaling

nv-power-27.claim: nvpmodel power modes cap memory/CPU/GPU frequencies and the number of online cores. The (unobserved) mode sets the ceiling on CPU/GPU and module power.
nv-power-27.relation: control: nvpmodel mode (unobserved per-device setting) bounds cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts
nv-power-27.quote: Capping the memory, CPU, and GPU frequencies, and number of online CPU, GPU TPC, DLA and PVA cores at a prequalified level confines the module to the target mode.
nv-power-27.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-28.claim: The power mode persists across power cycles, so it is a per-device constant (unless changed), not an hourly variable.
nv-power-28.relation: none (nvpmodel mode is static device context; unobserved)
nv-power-28.quote: After you set a power mode, the module stays in that mode until you change it. The mode persists across power cycles and SC7.
nv-power-28.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-29.claim: Orin Nano 8GB (4 GPU TPCs, default 15 W mode) and 4GB (2 GPU TPCs, default 10 W mode) differ in power budget, and Super flash configs default to 25 W. A mixed fleet would therefore have different power ceilings.
nv-power-29.relation: module SKU / flash config (unobserved) shifts the cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts ranges
nv-power-29.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 8GB ... GPU TPC | 4 | 2 | 4 | 4 | 4 ... * The default mode is 15W (mode ID 0). * The default mode is 25W (mode ID 1). ... Jetson Orin Nano 4GB ... GPU TPC | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 ... * The default mode is 10W (mode ID 0).
nv-power-29.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-29.section: Supported Modes and Power Efficiency > NVP Model Clock Configuration

nv-power-30.claim: Even in MAXN mode, hardware throttling engages when total module power exceeds the TDP budget. Module power is regulated, not free-running.
nv-power-30.relation: control: orin_power_watts (VDD_IN) regulated toward TDP budget by HW throttling
nv-power-30.quote: However, this mode does not guarantee the best performance for all use cases because hardware throttling is engaged when the total module power exceeds the TDP budget.
nv-power-30.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-31.claim: jetson_clocks pins CPU, GPU and EMC at static maximum frequencies. If BusPas runs it, the load -> frequency -> power dependence weakens and idle power rises.
nv-power-31.relation: conditional: if jetson_clocks used, cpu_gpu_power_watts depends less on workload (DVFS disabled)
nv-power-31.quote: The jetson_clocks.sh script maximizes a Jetson Orin performance by setting the static maximum frequencies of the CPU, GPU and EMC clocks.
nv-power-31.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-32.claim: Above a thermal trip point, software throttling uses DVFS to cut clock frequency and rail voltage, which reduces power. This is the documented reverse of 'power heats the die' and makes a lag-0 cycle, so it is a feedback note.
nv-power-32.relation: control (feedback note): cpu_temp_celsius/gpu_temp_celsius above trip -> lower clocks and voltage -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-32.quote: clock throttling employs the DVFS capabilities of the clocks to reduce their operating frequencies, and thereby the voltages of the rails that power the clocks. This reduction in frequency and voltage reduces power consumption which helps to control the temperature.
nv-power-32.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-33.claim: On Orin NX/Nano, the cpu-thermal and gpu-thermal zones start software throttling at 99.0 C (hardware throttling 103 C, shutdown 104.5/105 C). This documented ceiling matches the cluster of CPU readings near 99 C.
nv-power-33.relation: control: cpu_temp_celsius >= 99 C -> software throttling of CPU/GPU/EMC -> cpu_gpu_power_watts reduced (regulated ceiling on temperature)
nv-power-33.quote: cpu-thermal | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_CPU | SW throttling | 99.0 °C | 112.0 °C | HW throttling | 103.0 °C | 116.0 °C | SW shutdown | 104.5 °C | 117.5 °C | HW shutdown | 105.0 °C | 118.0 °C
nv-power-33.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-33.section: Thermal Specifications (column: Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Orin NX / Nano series)

nv-power-34.claim: The example gpu-thermal zone polls during passive throttling every 0x3e8 = 1000 ms. My reading of the units follows the kernel thermal-zone binding, which uses ms. The temperature-throttling loop runs at second scale, with no hour-scale delay to justify a lag-1 edge.
nv-power-34.relation: timing: throttle loop ~1 s -> keep as feedback note, not lag-1 edge
nv-power-34.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-34.section: Linux Thermal Framework > Configuring a Thermal Zone Using the Device Tree

nv-power-35.claim: NVIDIA's design uses the fan as the first line of defence to delay clock throttling. The signs have no fan, so clock throttling is the first active response, and the temperature-to-power feedback engages at lower power than on a cooled dev kit (inference).
nv-power-35.relation: feedback note: fanless -> throttling is the only active cooling, cpu_temp_celsius regulated via cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-35.quote: SoC thermal management uses the fan as the first line of defense to delay clock throttling until a much higher temperature is reached.
nv-power-35.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-36.claim: Runtime power management may switch off the GPU rail at idle, and the GPU sensor then cannot be read (-EAGAIN). An idle GPU therefore causes gpu_temp_celsius to be missing rather than low, depending on how the agent records failures.
nv-power-36.relation: GPU idle (e.g. deepstream_running = 0, inferred) -> gpu_temp_celsius unreadable/missing
nv-power-36.quote: The GPU, CV power rails might be turned off at idle by run time power management. The temperature cannot be read from GPU, CV thermal sensors when the power is off. Attempts to read a sensor with the power off will return error code -EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable).
nv-power-36.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-36.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Sensors and Sensor Groups

nv-power-37.claim: In the Active state the GPU rail can be powered off and the GPU power-gated. GPU idle therefore lowers CPU/GPU rail power toward the CPU-only level.
nv-power-37.relation: control: GPU idle -> VDD_GPU off / power-gated -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-power-37.quote: Many SoC devices may be idle or disabled under driver control. For example, VDD_GPU may be powered off and the companion GPU may be power-gated.
nv-power-37.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-37.section: Chipset Power States > Power State Mapping to Linux

nv-power-38.claim: CPU and GPU temperatures both come from SOC_THERM on-chip ring-oscillator sensors on the same die (center of CPU cluster, center of GPU). They share causes (SoC power, ambient), so they are redundant sensors of one die temperature field.
nv-power-38.relation: redundancy: cpu_temp_celsius ~ gpu_temp_celsius (same die, shared heat source)
nv-power-38.quote: SOC_THERM is the collection of on-chip ring oscillators whose frequency changes are based on temperature. ... CPU | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_CPU | Center of CPU cluster | GPU | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_GPU | Center of GPU
nv-power-38.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-38.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Thermal Sensing / SOC_THERM

nv-power-39.claim: Orin NX/Nano have no TMP451 board sensor, so the Jetson exposes no board-temperature sensor of its own. board_temp_celsius comes from BusPas's INA238 and has no NVIDIA-documented link to module power.
nv-power-39.relation: none (no NVIDIA board sensor; board_temp_celsius is outside this source)
nv-power-39.quote: There is no TMP451 thermal sensor on Jetson Orin NX and Jetson Orin Nano.
nv-power-39.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-39.section: Thermal Management in Linux > On-board Sensors

nv-power-40.claim: Jetson Power GUI shows per-channel instantaneous and average power, plus voltage, current and current limits. It confirms that an averaged power figure exists alongside instantaneous V/I/P, but it is only a display tool.
nv-power-40.relation: none (tool); per-channel V, I, P and averaged power are available on device
nv-power-40.quote: Instantaneous power read by power monitor | Average power read by power monitor | Reset average power calculation by clicking the "reset avg" button
nv-power-40.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)

nv-power-41.claim: tegrastats reports current and average power in mW for each INA3221 rail. If the heartbeat service gets cpu_gpu_power_watts or device_power_watts from tegrastats, they are VDD_CPU_GPU_CV and some other rail, possibly averaged (inferred).
nv-power-41.relation: possible definitional source (inferred): heartbeat cpu_gpu_power_watts/device_power_watts = tegrastats VDD_* current or average mW
nv-power-41.quote: VDDX Y /Z | VDDRQ 312/234 | Power consumption statistics for a power block. | Name of the power rail * | Block’s current power consumption in milliwatts | Block’s average power consumption in milliwatts
nv-power-41.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Tegrastats Utility

nv-power-42.claim: tegrastats documents that CPU frequency moves with CPU workload, which corroborates the load -> frequency -> power path.
nv-power-42.relation: control: CPU workload -> CPU frequency (-> cpu_gpu_power_watts via DVFS)
nv-power-42.quote: CPU frequency in megahertz. Goes up or down dynamically depending on the CPU workload.
nv-power-42.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Tegrastats Utility

nv-power-43.claim: In Deep Sleep (SC7), VDD_CORE and VDD_CPU are off and only RTC, DDR-IO, SYS-IO and DRAM rails stay on. If signs ever suspend, module power drops sharply; whether they do is unknown.
nv-power-43.relation: conditional: SC7 suspend -> orin_power_watts near floor (BusPas to confirm whether SC7 is used)
nv-power-43.quote: Deep Sleep (SC7) | Power rails: VDD_RTC, VDDIO_DDR, VDDIO_SYS, and DRAM power rails are powered on. VDD_CORE and VDD_CPU are powered off.
nv-power-43.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3 - Jetson Orin Nano/NX/AGX Orin Series (Platform Power and Performance)
nv-power-43.section: Chipset Power States > Supported Power States

nv-power-44.claim: The r38.x Developer Guide does not cover Orin; it covers Jetson Thor only, and the r38.2/r38.4 Orin page URLs return 404. The Orin-relevant versions are r36.x, plus r39.2.1, which keeps the same Orin text.
nv-power-44.quote: Version 38.2.1 of Jetson Linux does not support the Jetson Orin™ product family, including Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Orin NX, and Jetson Orin Nano. For Jetson Orin support, refer to the 36.4.4 GA release of the Jetson Linux Developer Guide.
nv-power-44.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide r38.2.1 (home page)

nv-thermal-1.claim: The CPU and GPU temperatures come from on-chip SOC_THERM sensors on the same Orin SoC die, at the centre of the CPU cluster and at the centre of the GPU.
nv-thermal-1.relation: redundancy: cpu_temp_celsius ~ gpu_temp_celsius (two sensors on one die, shared cause = die temperature)
nv-thermal-1.quote: CPU | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_CPU | Center of CPU cluster | GPU | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_GPU | Center of GPU
nv-thermal-1.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-1.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Thermal Sensing (table rows)

nv-thermal-2.claim: NVIDIA defines the junction temperature Tj as the die temperature read from any of the SoC's internal sensors, so the CPU and GPU readings are both measurements of Tj. A suggested redundancy direction is cpu_temp -> gpu_temp, because the GPU sensor is unavailable when the GPU is power-gated.
nv-thermal-2.quote: The NVIDIA Orin SoC junction temperature (Tj) represents the Orin SoC die temperature read from any of the internal temperature sensors. T.SoC refers to the junction temperature.
nv-thermal-2.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-3.claim: The on-die sensors sit near dominant hotspots, and a built-in hardware controller reads them to engage thermal protection.
nv-thermal-3.relation: cpu_temp_celsius and gpu_temp_celsius are inputs to thermal control (throttling, shutdown)
nv-thermal-3.quote: On the Orin SoC, there are multiple on-die temperature sensors that are placed close to dominant hotspots for real-time measurements of junction temperature. A built-in hardware controller is used to read the sensors and engage thermal protection mechanisms.
nv-thermal-3.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-4.claim: Argues against an exact CPU/GPU redundancy: different workloads load different parts of the die, so the hotspot moves and the CPU-GPU temperature gap depends on how work is split between CPU and GPU (for example, whether DeepStream drives the GPU).
nv-thermal-4.relation: the redundancy residual cpu_temp_celsius - gpu_temp_celsius depends on the workload mix (non-uniform die heating)
nv-thermal-4.quote: The variation between applications will cause variation in heat loads on the different components on the Jetson Orin module. It will also cause hotspots in different logical partitions of the Orin SoC.
nv-thermal-4.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-5.claim: Each zone reading is the maximum over a group of ring-oscillator sensors near that block, reported with 0.5 C precision.
nv-thermal-5.relation: measurement model: zone temperature = max of sensors in the group
nv-thermal-5.quote: The BPMP firmware reports the temperature of a given group by taking the maximum of all the sensors in the group.
nv-thermal-5.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-6.claim: NVIDIA states the Tj sensor accuracy as +/-3 C. This bounds how closely the CPU and GPU readings can agree and blurs the trip points.
nv-thermal-6.relation: sensor error +/-3 C (residual tolerance for the cpu/gpu redundancy)
nv-thermal-6.quote: The customer’s tolerance for performance reduction should determine the amount of Tj operating headroom in the thermal solution design to accommodate the temperature sensor accuracy of ± 3°C.
nv-thermal-6.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-7.claim: tj-thermal is a virtual sensor equal to the maximum of the CPU, GPU, CV and SOC sensors. It is not in the node list, but by definition it is at least as high as cpu_temp and gpu_temp.
nv-thermal-7.relation: none (tj = max(CPU, GPU, CV0-2, SOC0-2) is not measured; cpu_temp_celsius <= tj)
nv-thermal-7.quote: TJ_MAX | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_TJ_MAX | Virtual sensor corresponding to the highest temperature among CPU, GPU, CV0, CV1, CV2, SOC0, SOC1 and SOC2
nv-thermal-7.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-7.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Thermal Sensing

nv-thermal-8.claim: The GPU (and CV) rails can be power-gated at idle, and the GPU sensor cannot then be read. gpu_temp is therefore missing or invalid whenever the GPU is unused, so its validity depends on GPU activity. The link to deepstream_running is inferred.
nv-thermal-8.relation: gpu_temp_celsius undefined when the GPU rail is power-gated (GPU idle)
nv-thermal-8.quote: The GPU, CV power rails might be turned off at idle by run time power management. The temperature cannot be read from GPU, CV thermal sensors when the power is off. Attempts to read a sensor with the power off will return error code -EAGAIN (Resource temporarily unavailable).
nv-thermal-8.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-9.claim: NVIDIA staff say the thermal zone and tegrastats report -256 C when the engine is unused and power-gated. Another staff post (KevinFFF, thread 246051) gives -256000 m°C as the sysfs value. This matches the README's -256 GPU readings as a power-gating artefact rather than a temperature.
nv-thermal-9.relation: gpu_temp_celsius = -256 is a sentinel for 'GPU power-gated', not a temperature
nv-thermal-9.quote: Please check Jetson AGX Orin FAQ Q: Why thermal zone/tegrastats reports -256C? If the engine is not in-use, it is power gated and there is no thermal information.
nv-thermal-9.doc_title: NVIDIA forum: Jtop doesn't detect GPU temperature consistently (DaneLLL, NVIDIA Employee)

nv-thermal-10.claim: On Orin Nano the CV0-CV2 zones (DLA and PVA) are always offline because the chip has no DLA or PVA. Only the CPU, GPU, SOC0-2 and tj zones are meaningful.
nv-thermal-10.relation: none (cv zones do not exist on Orin Nano)
nv-thermal-10.quote: The CV0, CV1, and CV2 offline on Orin Nano are expected and not a bug. CV0, 1 refers to DLA0, DLA1 temperature, and CV2 refers to PVA temperature. Since Orin Nano doesn’t have DLA and PVA, it’s expected to see it shown as “offline”.
nv-thermal-10.doc_title: NVIDIA forum: Offline cv0, cv1 and cv2 (AastaLLL, NVIDIA Employee)

nv-thermal-11.claim: In every Orin Nano power mode the DLA and PVA core counts are 0. On Nano, the VDD_CPU_GPU_CV rail therefore effectively powers the CPU and GPU only, which supports reading cpu_gpu_power_watts as CPU+GPU power (inferred).
nv-thermal-11.relation: on Orin Nano, cpu_gpu_power_watts (if = VDD_CPU_GPU_CV) covers CPU + GPU cores only
nv-thermal-11.quote: NVP Model Clock Configuration for Jetson Orin Nano 4GB ... DLA cores | 0 | 0 | 0 ... PVA cores | 0 | 0 | 0
nv-thermal-11.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-11.section: Supported Modes and Power Efficiency (nvpmodel tables, Orin Nano 4GB and 8GB)

nv-thermal-12.claim: On the module's INA3221, channel 1 (VDD_IN) is total module power and channel 2 (VDD_CPU_GPU_CV) is CPU/GPU/CV power, so CPU+GPU power is part of module power. Mapping these channels to orin_power_watts and cpu_gpu_power_watts is inferred.
nv-thermal-12.relation: containment: cpu_gpu_power_watts is part of orin_power_watts (if they are VDD_CPU_GPU_CV and VDD_IN)
nv-thermal-12.quote: Channel 1: VDD_IN | Total Module Power | Channel 2: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV | Total power consumed by CPU, CPU and CV cores i.e. DLA and PVA | Channel 3: VDD_SOC | Power consumed by SOC core which supplies to memory subsystem and various engines
nv-thermal-12.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-12.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-thermal-13.claim: The heat load that sets module temperature is the total module power (TMP), defined as average dissipation in steady state. The guide gives only steady-state, not transient, relations.
nv-thermal-13.relation: heat source P in the module thermal network = total module power (orin_power_watts if it is VDD_IN)
nv-thermal-13.quote: The total module power (TMP) represents the average board power dissipation while the system is running the target workload under the worst-case conditions in steady state.
nv-thermal-13.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-14.claim: NVIDIA models the junction temperature with a thermal-resistance network from Tj to the ambient of the thermal solution: Tj = T_amb + R_j-a x TMP. Module power and the ambient around the heat sink both raise the die temperature. enclosure_temperature can stand in for T_amb only if it measures the air or wall the heat sink rejects heat into (unconfirmed).
nv-thermal-14.relation: physical: orin_power_watts heats cpu_temp_celsius and gpu_temp_celsius; enclosure_temperature -> cpu_temp_celsius, gpu_temp_celsius (additive offset, steady state)
nv-thermal-14.quote: A simple example of a thermal resistance network is shown in Figure 3-1, where Rj-a represents the thermal resistance from Tj to the ambient of the system thermal solution.
nv-thermal-14.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)
nv-thermal-14.section: 3.1.1 Jetson Orin Module Thermal Performance, Figure 3-1

nv-thermal-15.claim: The thermal resistance is defined as R1-2 = (T1 - T2)/P, where P is the dissipated power, so the temperature rise above ambient is linear in dissipated power.
nv-thermal-15.relation: cpu_temp_celsius - T_amb = R_j-a x P (linear, steady state)
nv-thermal-15.quote: R1-2 The thermal resistance between Point 1 and Point 2 / Tn The temperature at Point n / P The heat load (i.e; dissipated power) transferred between Points 1 and 2
nv-thermal-15.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)
nv-thermal-15.section: 3.1.1 (equation and symbol list; the PDF renders the symbols as images)

nv-thermal-16.claim: In the guide's worked example (T_amb = 55 C, target T.SoC = 95 C, TMP = 25 W), the required R_j-a is 1.60 C/W, which confirms the additive ambient + R x P form.
nv-thermal-16.quote: The required system thermal performance can be determined based on the ambient temperature conditions and TMP level required by the customer. ... In this example, a 1.60 °C/W thermal solution is expected to be sufficient to maintain the Orin SoC within the maximum temperature specification
nv-thermal-16.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-17.claim: The module has no thermal solution of its own. R_j-a, the power-to-temperature coefficient, is set entirely by BusPas's heat sink and enclosure design, which is undocumented here.
nv-thermal-17.relation: coefficient of orin_power_watts -> cpu_temp_celsius is device-design specific (unknown R_j-a)
nv-thermal-17.quote: The Jetson Orin module is not equipped with a system level thermal solution to dissipate the TMP thermal load into the ambient environment. It is the customer’s responsibility to design an adequate thermal solution
nv-thermal-17.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-18.claim: The SoC dissipates most of the total module power, so most of the heat that reaches the die sensors comes from the SoC rails (CPU/GPU/SOC).
nv-thermal-18.relation: physical: SoC power (incl. cpu_gpu_power_watts) dominates heating of cpu_temp_celsius and gpu_temp_celsius
nv-thermal-18.quote: Good contact of the thermal solution to the Orin SoC is critical for maximizing the thermal performance of the Jetson Orin module. The Orin SoC consumes the majority of the TMP.
nv-thermal-18.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-19.claim: Argues against a single fixed power-to-temperature coefficient: thermal performance depends on how evenly power is spread over the module, so the same total power can give different die temperatures for different CPU/GPU mixes.
nv-thermal-19.relation: effective R_j-a varies with the power distribution (both orin_power_watts and cpu_gpu_power_watts may be needed as parents)
nv-thermal-19.quote: While the system thermal solution will help to spread the heat and make the thermal performance as consistent as possible, different applications will have different levels of thermal performance. The more evenly the module power is distributed across the Jetson Orin module the higher the thermal
nv-thermal-19.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-20.claim: Orin Nano 4GB worst-case thermal loads: 10 W mode, total dissipated 8.87 W (SoC 6.90 W, Rj-c 0.218 C/W, Rj-b 1.722 C/W); 25 W MAXN_Super mode, total 23.6 W (SoC 20.20 W). NVIDIA labels these figures preliminary, computed at 5 V module input and under uniform die heating.
nv-thermal-20.relation: upper bound on module/SoC power per power mode (Orin Nano 4GB)
nv-thermal-20.quote: Table 3-12. Jetson Orin Nano 4GB Thermal Performance for 10 W Operational Mode ... 1 Orin SoC 1 6.90 6.90 0.218 1.722 - - ... 8.87 = Total Dissipated Power
nv-thermal-20.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)
nv-thermal-20.section: Table 3-12 (also Table 3-11: 25 W mode, SoC 20.20 W, total 23.6 W)

nv-thermal-21.claim: Orin Nano 8GB worst-case thermal loads: 7 W mode, total 6.77 W (SoC 5.00 W); 15 W mode, total 15.06 W (SoC 11.80 W, Rj-c 0.187 C/W, Rj-b 1.689 C/W); 25 W MAXN_Super mode, total 24.54 W (SoC 20.20 W).
nv-thermal-21.relation: upper bound on module/SoC power per power mode (Orin Nano 8GB)
nv-thermal-21.quote: Table 3-9. Jetson Orin Nano 8GB Thermal Performance for 15 W Operational Mode ... 1 Orin SoC 1 11.80 11.80 0.187 1.689 - - ... 15.06 = Total Dissipated Power
nv-thermal-21.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-22.claim: The thermal tables assume uniform heating of the die, which NVIDIA says is not true in practice, and NVIDIA calls them preliminary estimates.
nv-thermal-22.relation: caveat: the per-mode thermal numbers are approximate; the die is non-uniformly heated
nv-thermal-22.quote: Thermal model for Orin package is based on "Uniform heat loading of die.” In practice, the die will be non-uniformly loaded depending on the type of workload running on the die.
nv-thermal-22.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)
nv-thermal-22.section: Notes to Tables 3-1 to 3-12 (note 3; note 4: preliminary estimates)

nv-thermal-23.claim: Orin Nano power modes in nvpmodel: 4GB supports 10W (default, mode 0), 7W_AI and 7W_CPU; 8GB supports 15W (default), 7W and MaxN (super flash only). Each mode caps CPU/GPU/EMC frequencies and core counts. The active mode is an unobserved context that sets the power budget.
nv-thermal-23.relation: none (power mode is unobserved; it bounds orin_power_watts and cpu_gpu_power_watts)
nv-thermal-23.quote: Capping the memory, CPU, and GPU frequencies, and number of online CPU, GPU TPC, DLA and PVA cores at a prequalified level confines the module to the target mode.
nv-thermal-23.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-24.claim: Trip points for the cpu-thermal, gpu-thermal, cv0-2 and soc0-2 zones on Orin NX/Nano: SW throttling at 99.0 C, HW throttling at 103.0 C, SW shutdown at 104.5 C, HW shutdown at 105.0 C. The values are identical in r35.4.1, r36.4, r36.5 and r39.2.
nv-thermal-24.relation: control thresholds on cpu_temp_celsius/gpu_temp_celsius: 99.0 (SW throttle), 103.0 (HW throttle), 104.5 (SW shutdown), 105.0 (HW shutdown)
nv-thermal-24.quote: cpu-thermal | TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_CPU | SW throttling | 99.0 °C | ... | HW throttling | 103.0 °C | ... | SW shutdown | 104.5 °C | ... | HW shutdown | 105.0 °C
nv-thermal-24.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-24.section: Thermal Specifications (column Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Orin NX / Nano series)

nv-thermal-25.claim: The TDG specifies a maximum operating temperature of T.SoC = 99 C, above which software reduces clocks, and a shutdown temperature of 105 C. Short power spikes that push Tj over the threshold cause temporary clock reductions.
nv-thermal-25.relation: control: cpu_temp_celsius >= 99 C -> clock reduction lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts (feedback note)
nv-thermal-25.quote: Software will apply clock speed reductions after this temperature is reached. Note that power fluctuations that induce Tj fluctuations above these thresholds will cause temporary clock reductions.
nv-thermal-25.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)
nv-thermal-25.section: Table 2-1 Jetson Orin Module Thermal Specifications (note 1)

nv-thermal-26.claim: Software throttling uses DVFS to lower clock frequency and rail voltage, which lowers power and therefore temperature. With the power -> temperature heating this forms a lag-0 cycle, so it belongs in a feedback note, not an edge.
nv-thermal-26.relation: feedback note: cpu_temp_celsius/gpu_temp_celsius above trip -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts (and orin_power_watts) -> lower temperature
nv-thermal-26.quote: clock throttling employs the DVFS capabilities of the clocks to reduce their operating frequencies, and thereby the voltages of the rails that power the clocks. This reduction in frequency and voltage reduces power consumption which helps to control the temperature.
nv-thermal-26.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-27.claim: The software throttling cooling devices cap the CPU, GPU and EMC (memory controller) clocks, so throttling lowers SOC and memory power as well as CPU/GPU power.
nv-thermal-27.relation: feedback note: throttling caps CPU, GPU and EMC clocks -> lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts and the rest of orin_power_watts
nv-thermal-27.quote: Each of these cooling devices provides several cooling states, each of which translates to a maximum allowable operating frequency for the CPU, GPU, and EMC clocks.
nv-thermal-27.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-28.claim: The passive (throttling) loop polls every 1000 ms (0x3e8). Throttling acts on a time scale of seconds, far below one hour, so no source supports a lag-1 edge: within an hourly mean, temperature and power settle together.
nv-thermal-28.relation: feedback within the hour (lag 0): write it as a feedback note, not a lag-1 edge
nv-thermal-28.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-28.section: Configuring a Thermal Zone Using the Device Tree (example)

nv-thermal-29.claim: The software thermal management loop polls temperature, computes a throttle degree and caps CPU/GPU frequency, and stays active until temperature drops back below the threshold. Under sustained overload this holds the die near the 99 C trip, so temperature saturates instead of rising linearly with demanded power.
nv-thermal-29.relation: control: power -> temperature becomes non-linear and saturates near 99 C once throttling engages
nv-thermal-29.quote: Throttling is applied through limits on the clock frequency of high-power units such as the CPU and GPU. Higher throttling degree results in lower frequency limits. DVFS policies operate within these frequency limits.
nv-thermal-29.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-30.claim: Throttling persists until the temperature is back below the threshold and the throttle degree is zero.
nv-thermal-30.relation: control: throttling remains active while cpu_temp_celsius >= threshold
nv-thermal-30.quote: Software thermal management remains in operation until the Orin SoC temperature has returned to a value below the throttling threshold and throttling degree has returned to zero.
nv-thermal-30.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-31.claim: If software throttling fails to hold the temperature, hardware thermal throttling engages at 103 C. It lowers temperature but cuts performance significantly, and its settings cannot be changed.
nv-thermal-31.relation: control (feedback note): cpu_temp_celsius >= 103 C -> hard clock cap -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-thermal-31.quote: If software thermal management is not able to maintain the Orin SoC temperature, then hardware thermal throttling will engage to prevent thermal shutdown. ... This will lower the Orin SoC temperature, but it will also significantly reduce the overall Orin SoC performance.
nv-thermal-31.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-32.claim: Hardware (BPMP) throttling is also triggered by electrical OC alarms (battery overcurrent, PMIC voltage drop, temperature spikes). The host OS is not notified, so throttling state is unobserved in OS-level telemetry; the OC event counters are the only trace.
nv-thermal-32.relation: none (hardware throttling state is unobserved; it lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts when active)
nv-thermal-32.quote: The firmware refers to these events as OC alarms, and triggers clock hardware throttling to handle them. ... The host OS is not notified of these events, but you can detect the drop in clock rates by using a performance measuring tool that samples the CPU cycle counters.
nv-thermal-32.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-32.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Hardware Throttling > Impact

nv-thermal-33.claim: Hardware throttling caps the CPU and GPU clocks at three levels (light 50%, medium 75%, heavy 87.5% clock throttled) to limit current draw.
nv-thermal-33.relation: control: hardware throttle level caps cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-thermal-33.quote: To manage peak current consumption, the firmware supports capping the CPU and GPU clocks at three levels (light, medium, and heavy), as described in the device tree bindings. Clock capping prevents the CPU and GPU from drawing more current than their voltage regulators can supply.
nv-thermal-33.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-33.section: Hardware Throttling > Throttle Points and Vector Configuration

nv-thermal-34.claim: On Orin NX/Nano, average and instantaneous power limits on the VDD_IN channel keep total module power within the TDP budget by hardware-throttling the CPU and GPU. Module power is therefore actively capped near the mode budget (lag-0 feedback note).
nv-thermal-34.relation: control (feedback note): orin_power_watts (if = VDD_IN) above the limit -> CPU/GPU hardware throttling -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts
nv-thermal-34.quote: For Jetson Orin NX series and Jetson Orin Nano series modules, the average and instantaneous power limits has been set for the VDD_IN channel to ensure that the total module power does not exceed the Thermal Design Power (TDP) budget.
nv-thermal-34.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-34.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-thermal-35.claim: Orin Nano 4GB TDP budget 10 W: an average VDD_IN power above 10 W triggers OC2 (CPU/GPU throttled 50%); instantaneous power above 15 W triggers OC3 (87.5%); module under-voltage near 4.5 V triggers OC1 (87.5%). Orin Nano 8GB: 15 W average / 20 W instantaneous, or 25 W with the super configuration.
nv-thermal-35.relation: control: VDD_IN power limits per module bound orin_power_watts
nv-thermal-35.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 4GB | 10W | VDD_IN Average Power: 10W | OC2 | CPU: 50% GPU: 50% | VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 15W | OC3 | CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5% | Under Voltage: approx. 4.5V | OC1 | CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5%

nv-thermal-36.claim: A critical trip (104.5 C) triggers an orderly OS shutdown. The device then stops reporting, and its compute power falls away.
nv-thermal-36.relation: control: cpu_temp_celsius >= 104.5 C -> software shutdown (telemetry gap)
nv-thermal-36.quote: A critical trip point triggers a software thermal shutdown. It allows the operating system to save its state and perform an orderly shutdown before a hardware thermal reset occurs.
nv-thermal-36.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-37.claim: Above 105 C the SoC halts through the PMIC (thermtrip). After this failsafe shutdown the module needs a manual power-on, so a sign could stay off until serviced, unless BusPas's carrier restarts it (unknown).
nv-thermal-37.relation: control: cpu_temp_celsius > 105 C -> hardware shutdown; module stays off until power-on
nv-thermal-37.quote: Failsafe thermal shutdown is guaranteed by using the SHUTDOWN signal directly from Orin SoC to the PMIC. After the failsafe shutdown, the user will have to manually turn the system on by pressing the power button or equivalent input.
nv-thermal-37.doc_title: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series Modules Thermal Design Guide (TDG-11127-001_v1.5)

nv-thermal-38.claim: In NVIDIA's design the fan is the first line of defence and delays throttling. The signs are fanless, so the only temperature-driven actuator on power is clock throttling from 99 C, with no fan power or fan-speed relation to model.
nv-thermal-38.relation: none for fan; without a fan, cpu_temp_celsius affects power only through throttling (>= 99 C)
nv-thermal-38.quote: SoC thermal management uses the fan as the first line of defense to delay clock throttling until a much higher temperature is reached.
nv-thermal-38.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-thermal-39.claim: The GPU zone also has an 'active' gpu-hot-surface trip at 70 C (0x11170 m°C, 8 C hysteresis), mapped to a hot-surface alert device rather than the frequency cooling devices. No source shows it changing power, so no control relation exists below 99 C.
nv-thermal-39.relation: none (70 C hot-surface trip raises an alert; no documented power effect)
nv-thermal-39.quote: gpu-hot-surface { temperature = <0x11170>; type = "active"; hysteresis = <0x1f40>; phandle = <0x1bd>; }; ... hot-surface-alert-map0 { trip = <0x1bd>; cooling-device = <0x1ba 0x1 0x1>; };
nv-thermal-39.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-39.section: Configuring a Thermal Zone Using the Device Tree (example)

nv-thermal-40.claim: The guide is internally inconsistent: the prose says gpu-sw-slowdown is crossed at 99.5 C, but the device-tree value 0x182b8 is 99000 m°C (99.0 C), as in the spec table. The prose also calls the passive governor PID, while the example sets step_wise. Use 99.0 C.
nv-thermal-40.relation: none (documentation discrepancy; SW throttle trip = 99.0 C)
nv-thermal-40.quote: Clock throttling is performed using the devfreq cooling device when the passive trip point, gpu-sw-slowdown, is crossed at 99.5 °C: ... gpu-sw-slowdown { temperature = <0x182b8>; type = "passive";
nv-thermal-40.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4
nv-thermal-40.section: Configuring a Thermal Zone Using the Device Tree; Governors

nv-thermal-41.claim: Orin NX/Nano modules have no TMP451 on-board sensor, so NVIDIA's board sensors (Tboard_tegra, Tdiode_tegra) do not exist. board_temp_celsius must come from BusPas's own hardware (the INA238 die, per the README), and NVIDIA documents no coupling between it and SoC power.
nv-thermal-41.relation: none from NVIDIA docs: board_temp_celsius is not a Jetson module sensor
nv-thermal-41.quote: There is no TMP451 thermal sensor on Jetson Orin NX and Jetson Orin Nano, so the Tboard_tegra and Tdiode_tegra sensors are not available.
nv-thermal-41.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r35.4.1
nv-thermal-41.section: Thermal Management in Linux > On-board Sensors (Note); same note in r36.4

nv-thermal-42.claim: An NVIDIA application engineer confirms the throttle point is 99 C and the shutdown point 105 C on the SoC die. With throttling disabled, the next event is shutdown.
nv-thermal-42.relation: control thresholds on cpu_temp_celsius/gpu_temp_celsius: 99 C throttle, 105 C shutdown
nv-thermal-42.quote: Thermal throttle : 99’C on SoC die Thermal shutdown : 105’C on SoC die ... If you disable throttle, then the next even will be just shutdown, which is not recommended in general use.
nv-thermal-42.doc_title: NVIDIA forum: Thermal Throttling (EricGggg, NVIDIA Employee / application engineer)

nv-thermal-43.claim: NVIDIA staff say the permissible ambient is set by the thermal solution, as long as Tj stays below 99 C with margin. This supports ambient and power jointly setting Tj; there is no separate fixed ambient limit for the module.
nv-thermal-43.relation: physical: enclosure_temperature (as heat-sink ambient) + thermal solution set cpu_temp_celsius
nv-thermal-43.quote: Actual operating temperature range will depend on your thermal solution. As long as you are able to keep Orin SOC Tj below 99C with some margin ... the thermal solution will decide the higher operating temperature limit in your design.
nv-thermal-43.doc_title: NVIDIA forum: Jetson Orin NX - Clarification on Maximum Ambient Temperature (sgursal, NVIDIA Employee)

nv-thermal-44.claim: NVIDIA shares only the steady-state worst-case power and thermal-resistance tables, with no specific heat or thermal mass, so no thermal time constant is documented. Whether an hourly mean is in thermal steady state is therefore not supported by an NVIDIA source.
nv-thermal-44.relation: none (no documented thermal time constant; no basis for a lag-1 thermal edge)
nv-thermal-44.quote: These are the worst case power that Jetson Orin NX 16G can generate and user can use these for their thermal simulation. ... These are all that NV can share with Jetson users
nv-thermal-44.doc_title: NVIDIA forum: Specific Heat for Jetson Orin NX Thermal design (EricGggg, NVIDIA Employee)
nv-thermal-44.section: Reply by EricGggg, 2026-05-05 (answering a request for specific heat / transient data)

nv-thermal-45.claim: In MAXN mode, hardware throttling engages whenever total module power exceeds the TDP budget. This is another power-driven throttle that does not depend on temperature.
nv-thermal-45.relation: control (feedback note): orin_power_watts > TDP -> hardware throttling of CPU/GPU
nv-thermal-45.quote: However, this mode does not guarantee the best performance for all use cases because hardware throttling is engaged when the total module power exceeds the TDP budget.
nv-thermal-45.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series - Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4

nv-module-1.claim: The INA3221 power monitor is on the Orin NX/Nano module itself, at I2C address 0x40. So orin_power_watts, if it reads this chip, is measured on the module, downstream of whatever converter the carrier board uses.
nv-module-1.relation: orin_power_watts is measured at the module (after the carrier DC-DC), not at the sign input
nv-module-1.quote: The Jetson Orin NX series and Jetson Orin Nano series modules have a 3-channel INA3221 power monitor at the 0x40 I2C address.
nv-module-1.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-1.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-module-2.claim: INA3221 channel 1 (VDD_IN) is total module power and channel 2 (VDD_CPU_GPU_CV) is the CPU+GPU+CV (DLA/PVA) rail. CPU/GPU/CV power is therefore a part of total module power. This applies if the BusPas metrics read ch1 and ch2, which is not documented.
nv-module-2.relation: containment: cpu_gpu_power_watts -> orin_power_watts (cpu_gpu is part of total module power)
nv-module-2.quote: Channel 1: VDD_IN Total Module Power Channel 2: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV Total power consumed by CPU, CPU and CV cores i.e. DLA and PVA
nv-module-2.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-2.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (table rows, whitespace normalised; 'CPU, CPU' is NVIDIA's typo for CPU, GPU)

nv-module-3.claim: The third INA3221 channel, VDD_SOC (not a node), carries the memory subsystem and the video engines (nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp). Video-decode and memory load therefore shows up in total module power but NOT in VDD_CPU_GPU_CV. This argues against routing all DeepStream load through cpu_gpu_power_watts and supports a direct path into orin_power_watts. That DeepStream uses NVDEC is inferred and not stated in this source.
nv-module-3.relation: orin_power_watts = cpu_gpu_power_watts + VDD_SOC (unobserved) + other module loads; deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts directly (via unobserved VDD_SOC), not only via cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-3.quote: Channel 3: VDD_SOC Power consumed by SOC core which supplies to memory subsystem and various engines like nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp etc.
nv-module-3.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-3.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-module-4.claim: The module data sheet confirms one three-channel INA on the Orin Nano module, measuring the CPU_GPU_CV rail, Core (SOC) and module input power.
nv-module-4.relation: orin_power_watts = module input power (on-module sensor); cpu_gpu_power_watts is a sub-rail of it
nv-module-4.quote: Jetson Orin Nano has a single three-channel INA that can measure power of CPU_GPU_CV combined rail, Core, and module input power.
nv-module-4.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-4.section: 2.0 Power and System Management > Power Domains/Islands

nv-module-5.claim: The INA3221 driver exposes rail voltage (mV) and current (mA) but no power node. Any orin_power_watts or cpu_gpu_power_watts value is therefore computed by software as voltage x current (or taken from a tool such as tegrastats). Which method BusPas uses is undocumented.
nv-module-5.relation: identity: orin_power_watts = VDD_IN rail voltage x VDD_IN rail current (both unobserved)
nv-module-5.quote: curr<j>_input Gets rail current in milliamperes. in<i>_input Gets rail voltage in millivolts.
nv-module-5.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-5.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling (sysfs naming table, whitespace normalised)

nv-module-6.claim: tegrastats reports per-rail current and average power in mW, using the INA3221 rail names. If the heartbeat service gets cpu_gpu_power_watts or device_power_watts from tegrastats, it reads the same INA3221 sensor as orin_power_watts (redundancy, not independent physics).
nv-module-6.relation: possible redundancy: heartbeat power fields may be tegrastats copies of INA3221 rails (unconfirmed)
nv-module-6.quote: VDD_GPU 10687mW/9815mW Power consumption statistics for a power block. Name of the power rail * Block's current power consumption in milliwatts Block's average power consumption in milliwatts
nv-module-6.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Tegrastats Utility

nv-module-7.claim: VDD_IN must come from the carrier board. Everything the carrier supplies that is not VDD_IN (display, modem, heater, sensors, carrier regulators) is outside the module's INA3221 measurement. So input power at the sign = module power + carrier loads + conversion losses.
nv-module-7.relation: containment: orin_power_watts -> input_power_watts (input_power_watts - orin_power_watts = carrier loads + DC-DC losses), provided the INA238 sits upstream of the module supply
nv-module-7.quote: VDD_IN must be supplied by the carrier board that the Jetson Orin Nano is designed to connect to. All Jetson Orin Nano interfaces are referenced to on-module voltage rails and no I/O voltage is required to be supplied to the module.
nv-module-7.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-7.section: 2.0 Power and System Management > Power Rails

nv-module-8.claim: The module and the carrier board have separate supplies. The carrier board's own supplies are enabled by the module's SYS_RESET* after the module power sequence completes, which confirms that carrier loads hang off supplies other than the module's VDD_IN.
nv-module-8.relation: containment: carrier-board supplies and module supply are separate branches under input_power_watts
nv-module-8.quote: Used as carrier board supply enable when driven high by the module when module power sequence is complete. Used to ensure proper power on/off sequencing between module and carrier board supplies.
nv-module-8.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-8.section: 2.0 Power and System Management, Table 17 (SYS_RESET* row)

nv-module-9.claim: The recommended module VDD_IN is 4.75-5.25 V (typ. 5 V) for MODULE_ID-low (Orin Nano) modules. A 12 V (11-14 V) or ~56 V sign input therefore cannot feed the Orin Nano module directly, and input_voltage_volts is not the module supply voltage.
nv-module-9.relation: none (no direct electrical identity): input_voltage_volts is separated from module VDD_IN by a carrier step-down converter
nv-module-9.quote: VDD_IN (MODULE_ID low) 4.75 5 5.25 V VDD_IN (MODULE_ID high) 4.75 - 20 V
nv-module-9.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-9.section: 4.0 DC Characteristics, Table 22: Recommended Operating Conditions (columns min/typ/max, whitespace normalised)

nv-module-10.claim: NVIDIA staff: the Orin Nano module takes 5 V only, and a 5-20 V supply goes to the carrier, which converts it. For BusPas this means a step-down (12 V->5 V, or 56 V->...->5 V) with conversion losses sits between the INA238 input measurement and the module.
nv-module-10.relation: containment with loss: input_power_watts >= orin_power_watts / converter efficiency; supply_56v changes the conversion path (and likely loss)
nv-module-10.quote: For Orin Nano module, it is 5V only. You can power carrier with 5-20V supply but power module with 5V only.
nv-module-10.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Jetson Orin Nano Input Voltage

nv-module-11.claim: NVIDIA staff: the 9-20 V input range belongs to the devkit carrier, which has an on-board converter, while the module itself is 5 V.
nv-module-11.relation: carrier DC-DC converter sits between input_voltage_volts and module VDD_IN
nv-module-11.quote: Yes, for Orin nano module, it is 5V. The 9-20V is for devkit carrier as there is a converter on board.
nv-module-11.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Jetson Orin Nano SOM Power Requirements

nv-module-12.claim: On the NVIDIA reference (devkit) carrier, the DC jack feeds a GS9230 DC-DC converter (VAIN 6-28 V, UVLO 5.5 V), and the carrier's supported input is 9-20 V. A ~56 V input is outside this reference design, so 56 V signs must use a different (BusPas-specific) converter chain.
nv-module-12.relation: reference carrier: DC-in -> GS9230 DC-DC -> 5 V system rail; 56 V path unknown
nv-module-12.quote: Checked again that 9V~20V is the range. You can see in the GS9230 data sheet that the VAIN range is 6~28V and VAIN_UVLO is 5.5V. VAIN is tied to VIN. So 5V can not be used for devkit carrier supply.
nv-module-12.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Jetson Orin Nano Input Voltage

nv-module-13.claim: NVIDIA staff: the power tree of a custom carrier is the designer's choice, and NVIDIA gives no recommendation. Nothing in NVIDIA documentation fixes how a BusPas sign's input reaches the module or what else it powers. This argues against assuming the devkit topology.
nv-module-13.relation: none documented by NVIDIA: carrier power tree (and thus carrier loads/losses) is BusPas-specific
nv-module-13.quote: Power delivery or power tree design for your bigger carrier board is your system design choice. We do not have any recommendation.
nv-module-13.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Jetson orin nano developer kit, external power

nv-module-14.claim: On the module, VDD_IN feeds the PMIC and other regulators. These step it down to the SoC rails, so the CPU/GPU/CV rail is downstream of VDD_IN.
nv-module-14.relation: module power tree: VDD_IN (orin_power_watts) -> PMIC/regulators -> VDD_CPU_GPU_CV (cpu_gpu_power_watts), VDD_SOC, ...
nv-module-14.quote: 251 VDD_IN Main power – Supplies PMIC and other registers Input 5V to 20V
nv-module-14.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-14.section: 2.0 Power and System Management, Table 17 (VDD_IN row; 'registers' is NVIDIA's wording, the 5V-20V range was later restricted to 5V for Orin Nano)

nv-module-15.claim: NVIDIA staff: VDD_IN is regulated down by on-module regulators to the voltages the module needs, which confirms the on-module conversion stage between VDD_IN and the SoC rails.
nv-module-15.relation: containment: cpu_gpu_power_watts (rail) plus on-module regulator losses are inside orin_power_watts
nv-module-15.quote: 5V or 20V is input voltage and then onboard voltage regulators regulate it down to the voltages needed by the module.
nv-module-15.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Logic voltage of the Jetson Orin Nano module when the power supply is 20V

nv-module-16.claim: The Orin module has its own PMIC, voltage regulators and power tree. The module power budgets (modes) are defined at the module level.
nv-module-16.relation: on-module power tree exists between VDD_IN and SoC rails (details not public)
nv-module-16.quote: Jetson Orin is designed with a high efficiency Power Management Integrated Circuit (PMIC), voltage regulators, and power tree to optimize power efficiency.
nv-module-16.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-17.claim: The on-module schematic (and so the exact power tree and INA3221 shunt placement) is not public.
nv-module-17.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Orin nano customer board power design

nv-module-18.claim: The SoC core rails (VDD_CORE, VDD_CPU, VDD_GPU, VDD_CV) are directly controlled by BPMP firmware. Their voltages, and so CPU/GPU rail power, are set by firmware DVFS (unobserved control).
nv-module-18.relation: control: firmware DVFS (unobserved) sets rail voltage/frequency that drive cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-18.quote: The SoC core power rails ( VDD_CORE , VDD_CPU , VDD_GPU , and VDD_CV ) are under the direct control of the BPMP firmware.
nv-module-18.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-18.section: Power management (rail control), near Chipset Power States

nv-module-19.claim: On Orin NX/Nano, average and instantaneous power limits on the INA3221 VDD_IN channel trigger hardware CPU/GPU clock throttling when module power exceeds the TDP budget. Module power thus caps CPU/GPU power within the same hour, which is a lag-0 feedback (write it as a feedback note, not an edge).
nv-module-19.relation: control (feedback note): orin_power_watts above power limit -> CPU/GPU throttling lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-19.quote: When the module power consumption exceeds the configured power limit, the module will perform hardware-based clock throttling on the GPU and CPU for a configurable period.
nv-module-19.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-19.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

nv-module-20.claim: The VDD_IN power limits per module and mode are: Orin Nano 8GB 15 W average / 20 W instantaneous (25 W in Super). For the Orin Nano 4GB the limits are 10 W / 15 W (25 W Super). These bound orin_power_watts according to the unobserved power mode and SKU.
nv-module-20.relation: upper bound on orin_power_watts set by module SKU and power mode (unobserved device constants)
nv-module-20.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 8GB 15W VDD_IN Average Power: 15W OC2 CPU: 50% GPU: 50% VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 20W OC3 CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5%
nv-module-20.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-20.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series: TDP limits table (whitespace normalised)

nv-module-21.claim: A module VDD_IN under-voltage of about 4.5 V (OC1) also triggers CPU/GPU throttling. This involves the module's ~5 V input, which is not a node, not the 12/56 V sign input.
nv-module-21.relation: control: unobserved module VDD_IN under-voltage -> CPU/GPU throttling lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-21.quote: Under Voltage: approx. 4.5V OC1 CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5%
nv-module-21.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-21.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series: TDP limits table

nv-module-22.claim: The over-current (OC) alarm events that trigger hardware throttling are described as rare and transient. This argues that OC throttling has little effect on hourly means, so no strong hourly control edge comes from it.
nv-module-22.relation: against: hardware OC throttling is transient, weak at hourly resolution
nv-module-22.quote: Like software throttling, hardware throttling may reduce performance. Because the triggering events are rare and transient in nature, though, the user experience is minimally impacted.
nv-module-22.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-23.claim: For Jetson Orin NX/Nano, the cpu-thermal zone starts software throttling at 99.0 C and hardware throttling at 103.0 C (SW shutdown 104.5 C, HW shutdown 105.0 C). gpu-thermal and cv-thermal use the same values. So cpu_temp_celsius near 99 C means throttling is active.
nv-module-23.relation: control (feedback note): cpu_temp_celsius/gpu_temp_celsius >= 99 C -> throttling lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-23.quote: Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Orin NX / Nano series Jetson AGX Orin Industrial cpu-thermal TEGRA234_THERMAL_ZONE_CPU SW throttling 99.0 °C 112.0 °C HW throttling 103.0 °C 116.0 °C SW shutdown 104.5 °C 117.5 °C HW shutdown 105.0 °C 118.0 °C
nv-module-23.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-23.section: Thermal Specifications (table, whitespace normalised; first value column = Orin NX/Nano)

nv-module-24.claim: Software clock throttling uses DVFS to lower frequency and rail voltage, which lowers power and so temperature. NVIDIA states both directions here: dissipated power raises temperature, and temperature-triggered throttling lowers power. That is a lag-0 feedback loop, so draw power -> temperature as the edge and record throttling as a feedback note.
nv-module-24.relation: physical: cpu_gpu_power_watts heats cpu_temp_celsius and gpu_temp_celsius; control (feedback note): temperature trip -> DVFS lowers cpu_gpu_power_watts
nv-module-24.quote: clock throttling employs the DVFS capabilities of the clocks to reduce their operating frequencies, and thereby the voltages of the rails that power the clocks. This reduction in frequency and voltage reduces power consumption which helps to control the temperature.
nv-module-24.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-25.claim: Passive throttling is governed by a PID controller, so once a trip point is reached temperature is actively regulated around it. Above the trip, cpu_temp_celsius is set by the controller and cannot be explained by power alone.
nv-module-25.relation: control: PID governor holds temperature near trip point by limiting cpu_gpu_power_watts (feedback note)
nv-module-25.quote: A governor implements a feedback control loop that keeps a Jetson device within a safe operating temperature range.
