While the Linux thermal framework provides many different governors, BSP provides a simple Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) controller for all passive throttling needs.
nv-module-25.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-26.claim: NVIDIA uses a fan as the first line of defence before clock throttling. In the fanless BusPas signs that stage is absent, so throttling is the only thermal control and engages directly at the trip points.
nv-module-26.relation: context: no fan, so temperature -> throttling -> cpu_gpu_power_watts is the only active thermal control
nv-module-26.quote: SoC thermal management uses the fan as the first line of defense to delay clock throttling until a much higher temperature is reached.
nv-module-26.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-27.claim: The module is designed to accept passive heat sinks and limits its own internal temperature with hardware and software methods. Passive-only cooling is supported, with temperature bounded by control.
nv-module-27.relation: control: module temperature is bounded by on-module thermal management
nv-module-27.quote: It has been designed so that an active or passive heat sink solution can be attached. The module contains various methods through hardware and software to limit the internal temperature to within operating limits.
nv-module-27.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-27.section: 2.0 Power and System Management > Thermal and Power Monitoring

nv-module-28.claim: If the module overheats it shuts down. An hour containing a thermal shutdown would show module (and input) power collapsing. The effect runs from temperature to power and likely appears in the same or next hour.
nv-module-28.relation: control: cpu_temp_celsius at shutdown limit -> orin_power_watts (and input_power_watts) drop (feedback note / possible lag 1)
nv-module-28.quote: Thermal Shutdown If the internal temperature of the Jetson Orin Nano module reaches an unsafe temperature, the hardware is designed to initiate a shutdown.
nv-module-28.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)
nv-module-28.section: 2.7.2 OFF State, Table 19: OFF State Events

nv-module-29.claim: The CPU thermal zone reports the maximum of several CPU-cluster sensors, so cpu_temp_celsius (if read from cpu-thermal) is a hottest-spot value, not an average.
nv-module-29.relation: definition: cpu_temp_celsius = max over CPU-cluster on-die sensors
nv-module-29.quote: The BPMP firmware reports the temperature of a given group by taking the maximum of all the sensors in the group.
nv-module-29.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-29.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Sensors and Sensor Groups

nv-module-30.claim: The GPU/CV rails can be power-gated at idle, and the GPU thermal sensor cannot be read while gated. gpu_temp_celsius may therefore be missing, or come only from active samples, when the GPU is idle, for example without DeepStream (inferred link).
nv-module-30.relation: measurement: gpu_temp_celsius availability depends on GPU activity (missingness, not a value edge)
nv-module-30.quote: The GPU, CV power rails might be turned off at idle by run time power management. The temperature cannot be read from GPU, CV thermal sensors when the power is off.
nv-module-30.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-30.section: Thermal Management in BPMP > Sensors and Sensor Groups (Note)

nv-module-31.claim: Orin NX/Nano modules have no TMP451 board-temperature sensor. board_temp_celsius therefore cannot be a module board sensor and must come from a carrier-side chip (the README says the INA238 die). NVIDIA documents no link between it and module power.
nv-module-31.relation: none (from NVIDIA docs): board_temp_celsius is a carrier-side sensor; any coupling to module power depends on BusPas board layout
nv-module-31.quote: There is no TMP451 thermal sensor on Jetson Orin NX and Jetson Orin Nano.
nv-module-31.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-31.section: Thermal Management in Linux > On-board Sensors (Note)

nv-module-32.claim: Memory-controller (EMC) frequency, and so memory power on VDD_SOC, scales with memory bandwidth usage, not with the amount of RAM allocated. This argues against an edge from mem_used_gb to module power.
nv-module-32.relation: against: mem_used_gb -> orin_power_watts not supported; EMC DVFS follows bandwidth, not occupancy
nv-module-32.quote: If current memory bandwidth usage exceeds 30%, the BPMP will scale up the EMC frequency, and if the memory bandwidth usage is lower than 20%, the BPMP will scale down the EMC frequency.
nv-module-32.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance
nv-module-32.section: Memory Power Management > EMC Frequency Scaling Policy

nv-module-33.claim: A power mode (nvpmodel) caps CPU/GPU/memory frequencies and online cores, and it persists until changed. It is a per-device constant (unobserved) that shifts the operating level of cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts.
nv-module-33.relation: control: unobserved power mode caps cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts (device-level context, not a node)
nv-module-33.quote: Capping the memory, CPU, and GPU frequencies, and number of online CPU, GPU TPC, DLA and PVA cores at a prequalified level confines the module to the target mode.
nv-module-33.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-34.claim: A power mode, once set, persists across power cycles and SC7. It is a stable per-device setting rather than something that varies hour to hour.
nv-module-34.relation: context: power mode is a persistent device constant (unobserved)
nv-module-34.quote: After you set a power mode, the module stays in that mode until you change it. The mode persists across power cycles and SC7.
nv-module-34.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

nv-module-35.claim: NVIDIA staff: the Orin Nano module data sheet gives a maximum VDD_IN current of 5 A, with 4.75-5.25 V recommended. At ~5 V this bounds orin_power_watts at about 25 W.
nv-module-35.quote: Note that the Jetson Orin Nano Series Module Data Sheet specifies VDD_IN I max as 5A.
nv-module-35.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Jetson Orin Nano 8GB - Voltage drop on SYS_5V under load

nv-module-36.claim: The design guide (quoted by NVIDIA staff) defines MODULE_ID: low means a legacy module with 5 V nominal VDD_IN, high means a wide-range (5-20 V) module. Orin Nano is the 5 V type.
nv-module-36.relation: none: module VDD_IN (5 V for Orin Nano) differs from sign input voltage; a carrier converter is needed
nv-module-36.quote: MODULE_ID indicates the capability of the module. Low: Legacy module with VDD_IN = 5V nominal. High: Advanced module supporting wide VDD_IN range (5V-20V).
nv-module-36.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forum: Orin NX power supply - benefit of using 20V? (quoting DG-10931-001)
nv-module-36.section: post #3 (Trumany, NVIDIA moderator, quoting the Design Guide)

nv-module-37.claim: In Deep Sleep (SC7) the CPU and core rails are powered off. If BusPas signs ever suspend, orin_power_watts would drop sharply for reasons outside the load nodes.
nv-module-37.relation: context: SC7 suspend (unobserved) drives module power near zero
nv-module-37.quote: Deep Sleep (SC7) Power rails : VDD_RTC , VDDIO_DDR , VDDIO_SYS , and DRAM power rails are powered on. VDD_CORE and VDD_CPU are powered off.
nv-module-37.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.5: Platform Power and Performance

ti-ina238-1.claim: The INA238 computes power on-chip from its own current result and its latest bus-voltage measurement, so input power per sample is defined as input voltage x input current.
ti-ina238-1.relation: input_power_watts = input_voltage_volts x input_current_amperes (identity, computed on-chip)
ti-ina238-1.quote: Power is calculated based on the previous current calculation and the latest bus voltage measurement.
ti-ina238-1.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-2.claim: The ADC measures only three things (shunt voltage, bus voltage, die temperature). Current and power are calculated from them, so input_voltage_volts and board_temp_celsius are primary measurements and input_current_amperes and input_power_watts are derived.
ti-ina238-2.relation: input_voltage_volts, board_temp_celsius = measured; input_current_amperes = V_shunt / R_shunt; input_power_watts = computed
ti-ina238-2.quote: The device measures shunt voltage, bus voltage and internal temperature while calculating current, power necessary for accurate decision making in precisely controlled systems.
ti-ina238-2.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-3.claim: With averaging on, the POWER register holds the average of per-sample products (mean of V*I), not the product of averaged V and I. So after hourly averaging, P = V x I holds only approximately: mean(V*I) = mean(V)*mean(I) + cov(V,I). The covariance step is my inference, not TI's text.
ti-ina238-3.relation: input_power_watts ~= input_voltage_volts x input_current_amperes at hourly means (approximate identity)
ti-ina238-3.quote: Following every measured sample, the newly-calculated values for current and power are appended to this accumulation register until all of the samples have been measured and averaged.
ti-ina238-3.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-4.claim: Current is not measured directly. It is calculated from the shunt voltage using the SHUNT_CAL constant, which encodes the shunt resistance.
ti-ina238-4.quote: Note that the current is calculated following a shunt voltage measurement based on the value set in the SHUNT_CAL register.
ti-ina238-4.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-5.claim: SHUNT_CAL must be reprogrammed after every power-up of the chip supply. If it is not set, current and power read zero while bus voltage stays valid. This is a documented failure signature, not a low load.
ti-ina238-5.relation: failure mode: input_current_amperes = input_power_watts = 0 while input_voltage_volts is valid
ti-ina238-5.quote: The shunt calibration register needs to be correctly programmed at each VS power up for the device to properly report any result based on current. Failure to set the value of the shunt calibration register results in a zero value for any result based on current.
ti-ina238-5.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-6.claim: The POWER register is unsigned and positive only, while CURRENT is two's complement (signed). If current ever reverses through the shunt, power stays positive while current goes negative, so the identity would become P = V x |I>. TI does not state this explicitly; it is inferred.
ti-ina238-6.relation: input_power_watts >= 0; if current can reverse, input_power_watts = input_voltage_volts x |input_current_amperes| (inferred)
ti-ina238-6.quote: Calculated power output. Output value in watts. Unsigned representation. Positive value.
ti-ina238-6.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-7.claim: The chip measures bidirectional current, so input_current_amperes can be negative if the monitored point sees reverse flow (for example battery charging). Bus voltage is always positive.
ti-ina238-7.relation: none (sign convention: input_current_amperes may be < 0; input_voltage_volts >= 0)
ti-ina238-7.quote: The shunt voltage measurement can be positive or negative due to bidirectional currents in the system; therefore the data value in VSHUNT can be positive or negative.
ti-ina238-7.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-8.claim: The Linux driver reads power1_input straight from the chip's 24-bit POWER register (it does not multiply V x I in software) and clamps the value at 0 or above.
ti-ina238-8.relation: input_power_watts (power1_input) = on-chip POWER register; identity computed in hardware, not by the driver

ti-ina238-9.claim: The bus-voltage input covers 0 to 85 V (common mode -0.3 to 85 V), so both the ~12 V and the ~55.9 V supplies are measured without clipping. supply_56v only shifts the operating level of input_voltage_volts.
ti-ina238-9.relation: supply_56v -> input_voltage_volts (sets the level, ~56 V vs ~12 V; no saturation)
ti-ina238-9.quote: Monitored bus voltages can range from 0 V to 85 V, while monitored temperatures can range from -40 ºC to +125 ºC.
ti-ina238-9.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-10.claim: Total power error is at most 0.7% of full scale over -40 to 125 C, and bus-voltage resolution is 3.125 mV/LSB. This bounds the chip-level residual of the P = V x I check, so larger residuals point to aggregation or software problems rather than the chip.
ti-ina238-10.relation: identity tolerance: |input_power_watts - input_voltage_volts x input_current_amperes| <~ 0.7% FS (per sample)
ti-ina238-10.quote: Power monitoring accuracy: – 0.7% full scale, –40°C to +125°C (maximum)
ti-ina238-10.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-11.claim: Conversion time is selectable from 50 us to 4.12 ms and averaging from 1x to 1024x. Even the slowest setting covers only about 4.2 s per input (Table 7-2), so each reading is a short-window snapshot, not a mean over the 120 s scrape interval.
ti-ina238-11.relation: none (sampling property: readings are short-window averages)
ti-ina238-11.quote: The device allows for selectable ADC conversion times from 50µs to 4.12ms as well as sample averaging from 1x to 1024x, which further helps reduce the noise of the measured data.
ti-ina238-11.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-12.claim: The mainline driver (v6.1 and current master) sets 16-sample averaging, 1052 us conversion on all three inputs, continuous mode. Each register value is then about a 50 ms average (3 x 1.052 ms x 16, my arithmetic), so a 120 s scrape sees about 0.04% of the interval. This holds only if BusPas uses this driver and these defaults.
ti-ina238-12.relation: none (sampling: ~50 ms window per reading under mainline defaults)
ti-ina238-12.quote: /* 16 sample averaging, 1052us conversion time, continuous mode */

ti-ina238-13.claim: The output registers hold the last completed result until the next one replaces it. There is no on-chip integration over the read interval, so anything that integrates power over time must be done in software.
ti-ina238-13.relation: input_energy_rate_w is not from an on-chip integral (argues against a hardware-energy relation)
ti-ina238-13.quote: These values remain in the data output registers until they are replaced by the next fully completed conversion results.
ti-ina238-13.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-14.claim: The INA238 has no energy or charge accumulator. Table 6-3 lists CONFIG, ADC_CONFIG, SHUNT_CAL, VSHUNT, VBUS, DIETEMP, CURRENT, POWER, DIAG_ALRT, limit and ID registers only; addresses 9h and Ah (ENERGY and CHARGE on the INA228) are unlisted, i.e. reserved. So input_energy_rate_w cannot come from the chip.
ti-ina238-14.relation: input_energy_rate_w = software integral of input power (not a hardware counter)
ti-ina238-14.quote: All register locations not listed in Table 6-3 must be considered as reserved locations and the register contents must not be modified.
ti-ina238-14.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-15.claim: The kernel documentation says energy is reported by the INA228 variant (and the INA700, INA780 and SQ52206), not by the INA238.
ti-ina238-15.relation: none from the chip (the INA238 hwmon device has no energy1_input)
ti-ina238-15.quote: INA228 is another variant of INA238 with higher ADC resolution. This chip also reports the energy.

ti-ina238-16.claim: The driver source marks the INA238 as having no energy register (has_energy = false), unlike the INA228, INA700, INA780 and SQ52206. Whitespace in the quote is collapsed.
ti-ina238-16.relation: none from the chip (no energy attribute for the INA238)

ti-ina238-17.claim: Consistent with the chip having no energy register, the README says the energy counter is computed on the device by integrating input power. Its hourly increase is therefore by definition the hourly mean input power, but it is computed by BusPas software at an unknown sampling rate and resets about daily. The README states its meanings are inferred.
ti-ina238-17.relation: input_energy_rate_w = hourly mean of integrated input power ~= input_power_watts (software identity; reset hours excluded)
ti-ina238-17.quote: Energy used, computed on the device by integrating input power over time. *Source: `calc:integrated_input_power`.*

ti-ina238-18.claim: The README describes input power as about input voltage x input current from the INA238. This meaning is inferred by the README authors, but it matches the datasheet's on-chip power calculation.
ti-ina238-18.quote: Power drawn at the device's input (about input voltage x input current). *Source: `sysfs:ina238`.*

ti-ina238-19.claim: board_temp_celsius is the INA238's die temperature. TI says it is useful for monitoring the system ambient temperature, so it tracks the local air and PCB temperature where the chip sits, presumably inside the enclosure.
ti-ina238-19.relation: enclosure_temperature -> board_temp_celsius (physical: die temperature follows local ambient)
ti-ina238-19.quote: The integrated temperature sensor is ±1°C accurate for die temperature measurement and is useful in monitoring the system ambient temperature.
ti-ina238-19.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-20.claim: The temperature register is the chip's internal die temperature (there is no external thermistor input) with 0.125 C resolution. The README's 'board temperature' is this die temperature.
ti-ina238-20.quote: Internal die temperature measurement. Two's complement value. Conversion factor: 125 m°C/LSB
ti-ina238-20.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-21.claim: The README names this metric a board temperature read from the INA238 chip (an inferred meaning), consistent with it being the INA238 die temperature.
ti-ina238-21.quote: Board temperature, read from the INA238 power-monitor chip. *Source: `sysfs:ina238`.*

ti-ina238-22.claim: The chip barely heats itself. Typical supply current is 640 uA; at VS = 3.3 V that is about 2.1 mW, so with PsiJB 97.6 C/W and RthetaJA 177.6 C/W the die runs about 0.2 C above the PCB and about 0.4 C above ambient (my arithmetic). board_temp_celsius is therefore not driven by the chip's own power or by the load current passing through it.
ti-ina238-22.relation: none: no self-heating edge input_power_watts/input_current_amperes -> board_temp_celsius through the INA238 itself (argues against)
ti-ina238-22.quote: Operational current: 640µA (typical) ... Junction-to-ambient thermal resistance 177.6 °C/W ... Junction-to-board characterization parameter 97.6 °C/W
ti-ina238-22.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-23.claim: TI's thermal-metrics note says the PCB carries 75-95% of a package's heat and gives TJ = T_PCB + PsiJB x P. The INA238 die temperature is therefore about the PCB temperature at the chip, and that PCB is warmed by whatever else dissipates nearby (regulators, possibly the Orin carrier or heater). The placement is not documented.
ti-ina238-23.relation: board_temp_celsius ~= local PCB temperature; candidate physical edges input_power_watts (or orin_power_watts) heats board_temp_celsius and enclosure_temperature -> board_temp_celsius (placement-dependent)
ti-ina238-23.quote: can allow the system designer to measure the board temperature with a fine gauge thermocouple and back-calculate the junction temperature using Equation 9. Note that ΨJB is close to Rθ(JB), as the PCB dissipates 75%–95% of the heat of a device.
ti-ina238-23.doc_title: Semiconductor and IC Package Thermal Metrics (TI application note SPRA953D)

ti-ina238-24.claim: The shunt resistor dissipates I^2 R. At the dataset's roughly 0.2-1.5 A and a milliohm-range shunt (actual value unknown), that is micro- to milliwatts (my arithmetic), so heat from the shunt does not materially affect the die sensor.
ti-ina238-24.relation: input_current_amperes heats the shunt (I^2 R) near board_temp_celsius: negligible (argues against an edge)
ti-ina238-24.quote: Also keep in mind that RSHUNT must be able to handle the power dissipated across the resistor in the maximum load condition.
ti-ina238-24.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-25.claim: Offset and gain drift are tiny (gain drift at most 25 ppm/C, offset drift at most 0.02 uV/C), so temperature does not materially bias the voltage, current or power readings. There is no measurement-artifact edge from board temperature into the INA238 readings.
ti-ina238-25.relation: none (argues against board_temp_celsius -> input_* measurement-artifact edges)
ti-ina238-25.quote: The low offset and gain drift design of the INA238 allows the device to be used in precise systems that do not undergo multi-temperature calibration during manufacturing.
ti-ina238-25.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-26.claim: Valid board_temp_celsius values lie between -40 and 125 C (accuracy 1 C at 25 C, 2 C over the full range). Values outside that range are invalid readings.
ti-ina238-26.quote: The internal die temperature sensor range extends from –256 °C to +256 °C but is limited by the package to –40 °C to 125 °C.
ti-ina238-26.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)
ti-ina238-26.section: 7.1.1 Device Measurement Range and Resolution; 5.5 Temperature sensor

ti-ina238-27.claim: VBUS is a separate pin measured against device ground, and TI recommends wiring it to the voltage powering the load. Which node it connects to on the BusPas board (supply input, battery, or MPPT load output) is a board design choice not documented here, so any redundancy with MPPT voltages is undetermined.
ti-ina238-27.relation: input_voltage_volts may be redundant with mppt_load_voltage or mppt_battery_voltage on has_solar devices, depending on undocumented wiring
ti-ina238-27.quote: Connect the VBUS pin to the voltage powering the load for load power calculations..
ti-ina238-27.doc_title: INA238 85V, 16-Bit, High-Precision Power Monitor With I2C Interface (TI datasheet SLYS025B)

ti-ina238-28.claim: The driver scales current and power by the same shunt-resistor value taken from the device tree. If none is set, the default is 10 mOhm in v6.1 and 2.5 mOhm in master. A wrong shunt setting therefore scales input_current_amperes and input_power_watts by one common factor while voltage is unaffected: P = V x I still holds, but cross-sensor relations (to orin_power_watts or mppt_load_power) would be off by a constant.
ti-ina238-28.relation: calibration: input_current_amperes and input_power_watts share one scale factor; input_voltage_volts independent
ti-ina238-28.quote: This scaling means the resulting values for Current and Power registers need to be scaled by the difference between the fixed shunt resistor and the actual shunt resistor

ti-ina238-29.claim: In hwmon, in1_input is the bus voltage and in0_input is the millivolt-level shunt voltage. input_voltage_volts (11-56 V) must therefore be in1_input / 1000.
ti-ina238-29.quote: in0_input Shunt voltage (mV) ... in1_input Bus voltage (mV)

ti-ina238-30.claim: sysfs exposes current in mA, power in uW and die temperature in milli-degrees C. The INA238 has no energy1_input attribute.
ti-ina238-30.relation: input_current_amperes = curr1_input/1e3; input_power_watts = power1_input/1e6; board_temp_celsius = temp1_input/1e3 (definitions)
ti-ina238-30.quote: curr1_input Current measurement (mA) ... power1_input Power measurement (uW) ... temp1_input Die temperature measurement (mC)

ti-ina3221-1.claim: Each INA3221 channel measures two raw quantities: the shunt voltage drop caused by the load current (between IN+ and IN-) and the bus voltage at IN- with respect to ground; any INA3221-based power figure is therefore derived from these two per-channel readings.
ti-ina3221-1.relation: measurement model: orin_power_watts derived from V_bus(ch) and V_shunt(ch) of one INA3221 channel (channel not documented)
ti-ina3221-1.quote: The voltage developed from the load current passing through a shunt resistor creates a shunt voltage that is measured between the IN+ and IN– pins. The device also internally measures the power-supply bus voltage at the IN– pin for each channel.

ti-ina3221-2.claim: The INA3221 has no power register and does not compute power on-chip; the Linux driver documentation states that current and power are computed on the host from the shunt and bus voltages.
ti-ina3221-2.relation: identity (software): orin_power_watts = V_bus(ch) x I(ch), computed host-side, not by the chip
ti-ina3221-2.quote: The INA3221 monitors both shunt drop and supply voltage, with programmable conversion times and averaging, current and power are calculated host-side from these.

ti-ina3221-3.claim: The INA3221 register set (Table 8-1) holds only configuration, per-channel shunt and bus voltages, alert limits, the shunt-voltage sum, mask/enable, power-valid limits and ID registers; there is no power register and no temperature register.
ti-ina3221-3.relation: none on-chip; power must be computed by software (see identity above)
ti-ina3221-3.quote: The INA3221 uses a bank of registers for holding configuration settings, measurement results, minimum and maximum limits, and status information.
ti-ina3221-3.section: 8 Register Maps / Table 8-1 Summary of Register Set

ti-ina3221-4.claim: AGAINST a sensor link: the INA3221 has no die-temperature measurement (its features list only shunt and bus voltage), so none of the temperature nodes, including board_temp_celsius (which the README attributes to the INA238), can come from the INA3221.
ti-ina3221-4.relation: none (no shared-sensor redundancy between orin_power_watts and any temperature node via the INA3221)
ti-ina3221-4.quote: Senses bus voltages from 0V to 26V • Reports shunt and bus voltage

ti-ina3221-5.claim: The Linux driver exposes per-channel bus voltage (mV) and current (mA) but no power attribute, so a metric labelled power with source sysfs:ina3221 must be a product (or sum) computed by the BusPas exporter; which product is inferred, not documented.
ti-ina3221-5.relation: identity (inferred): orin_power_watts = in<i>_input x curr<i>_input / 1e6 for some channel i
ti-ina3221-5.quote: in[123]_input Bus voltage(mV) channels curr[123]_input Current(mA) measurement channels shunt[123]_resistor Shunt resistance(uOhm) channels

ti-ina3221-6.claim: The driver converts the shunt-voltage register to current by dividing by the configured shunt resistance (I = V_shunt / R_shunt), so reported current scales with the device-tree shunt value.
ti-ina3221-6.quote: /* Scale of shunt voltage: LSB is 40uV (40000nV) */ voltage_nv = regval * 40000; /* Return current in mA */ *val = DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(voltage_nv, resistance_uo);

ti-ina3221-7.claim: On Jetson Orin NX and Orin Nano modules the single INA3221 at I2C 0x40 has channel 1 = VDD_IN, described as total module power; this is the most plausible rail behind a metric named orin_power_watts, but the channel actually read by BusPas is not documented.
ti-ina3221-7.relation: orin_power_watts plausibly = VDD_IN (channel 1) power = total Orin module power (inferred)
ti-ina3221-7.quote: The Jetson Orin NX series and Jetson Orin Nano series modules have a 3-channel INA3221 power monitor at the 0x40 I2C address. ... Channel 1: VDD_IN | Total Module Power
ti-ina3221-7.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-7.section: Software-Based Power Consumption Modeling > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

ti-ina3221-8.claim: Channel 2 (VDD_CPU_GPU_CV) carries CPU, GPU and CV-core (DLA, PVA) power and is part of the total module power on VDD_IN; if cpu_gpu_power_watts is this channel and orin_power_watts is VDD_IN, the CPU/GPU power is contained in the Orin power (the doc's text says 'CPU, CPU' — an apparent typo for CPU, GPU given the rail name).
ti-ina3221-8.relation: containment (conditional on channel mapping): cpu_gpu_power_watts -> orin_power_watts (part of)
ti-ina3221-8.quote: Channel 2: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV | Total power consumed by CPU, CPU and CV cores i.e. DLA and PVA
ti-ina3221-8.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-8.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (rail names for I2C address 0x40)

ti-ina3221-9.claim: Channel 3 (VDD_SOC) supplies the memory subsystem and the video/imaging engines (nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp); this rail is not a node, so video-pipeline load can raise module power (VDD_IN) without passing through cpu_gpu_power_watts, which justifies a direct edge from video-analytics context to orin_power_watts in addition to the path via cpu_gpu_power_watts (DeepStream's use of these engines needs a DeepStream source).
ti-ina3221-9.relation: orin_power_watts = cpu_gpu_power_watts + P(VDD_SOC, unobserved) + other module loads; deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts directly (via unobserved VDD_SOC) is not redundant with the cpu_gpu path
ti-ina3221-9.quote: Channel 3: VDD_SOC | Power consumed by SOC core which supplies to memory subsystem and various engines like nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp etc.
ti-ina3221-9.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-9.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (rail names for I2C address 0x40)

ti-ina3221-10.claim: NVIDIA sets average and instantaneous power limits on VDD_IN for Orin NX/Nano; when module power exceeds them, hardware clock throttling of CPU and GPU follows for a configurable period. This is a lag-0 negative feedback from module power onto CPU/GPU power and should be written as a feedback note, not an edge (no hour-scale delay is documented).
ti-ina3221-10.relation: control/feedback note: orin_power_watts above VDD_IN limit -> CPU/GPU clock throttling (unobserved) -> lower cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts (lag 0, not an edge)
ti-ina3221-10.quote: When the module power consumption exceeds the configured power limit, the module will perform hardware-based clock throttling on the GPU and CPU for a configurable period.
ti-ina3221-10.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-10.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (TDP limits)

ti-ina3221-11.claim: For the Jetson Orin Nano 8GB in its 15 W budget, the VDD_IN average-power limit (15 W) maps to SOCTHERM OC2 and the instantaneous limit (20 W) to OC3, with CPU/GPU throttled to 50% and 87.5% respectively.
ti-ina3221-11.relation: control threshold on orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN): avg > 15 W -> OC2 throttling; instantaneous > 20 W -> OC3 throttling
ti-ina3221-11.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 8GB | 15W | VDD_IN Average Power: 15W | OC2 | CPU: 50% GPU: 50% | VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 20W | OC3 | CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5%
ti-ina3221-11.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-11.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (TDP limits table; table cells joined with |)

ti-ina3221-12.claim: For the Jetson Orin Nano 4GB in its 10 W budget, the VDD_IN limits are 10 W average (OC2) and 15 W instantaneous (OC3), and a VDD_IN under-voltage of about 4.5 V raises OC1; the applicable limits depend on which module variant and power mode each sign runs.
ti-ina3221-12.relation: control threshold on orin_power_watts (if VDD_IN), module-variant dependent
ti-ina3221-12.quote: Jetson Orin Nano 4GB | 10W | VDD_IN Average Power: 10W | OC2 | CPU: 50% GPU: 50% | VDD_IN Instantaneous Power: 15W | OC3 | CPU: 87.5% GPU: 87.5% | Under Voltage: approx. 4.5V | OC1
ti-ina3221-12.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3
ti-ina3221-12.section: Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (TDP limits table; table cells joined with |)

ti-ina3221-13.claim: Hardware (OC) throttling is not reported to the host OS and is described as rare and transient, so the throttling state is unobserved in the telemetry and gives no basis for an hour-scale (lag-1) edge.
ti-ina3221-13.relation: none (throttling state unobserved; transient, no hour-scale lag)
ti-ina3221-13.quote: Because the triggering events are rare and transient in nature, though, the user experience is minimally impacted. The host OS is not notified of these events, but you can detect the drop in clock rates by using a performance measuring tool that samples the CPU cycle counters.
ti-ina3221-13.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3

ti-ina3221-14.claim: Orin has three OC event types (under-voltage, average overcurrent, instantaneous overcurrent) whose enable flags and counts are readable in sysfs; the telemetry does not include these counters, so they could only enter as a future context node.
ti-ina3221-14.quote: There are 3 types of OC events in the Orin series, which are Under Voltage, Average Overcurrent, and Instantaneous Overcurrent events respectively.
ti-ina3221-14.doc_title: Jetson Orin Nano Series, Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson AGX Orin Series — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3

ti-ina3221-15.claim: The INA3221 has two current alerts: Critical compares each single shunt conversion to a limit and Warning compares the averaged shunt value; both are disabled by default (limits at full scale) and only act when a limit is programmed, which NVIDIA does for VDD_IN.
ti-ina3221-15.relation: control trigger mechanism: per-conversion (critical) and averaged (warning) channel current over limit -> alert pin asserted
ti-ina3221-15.quote: The critical-alert feature monitors functions based on individual conversions of each shunt-voltage channel. ... At power-up, the default critical-alert limit value for each channel is set to the positive full-scale value, effectively disabling the alert.

ti-ina3221-16.claim: The Warning alert operates on the averaged shunt voltage, i.e. it flags a too-high average current, matching NVIDIA's 'average power' limit (OC2), while Critical matches the 'instantaneous' limit (OC3); this pin-to-OC mapping for Orin is inferred by matching, not stated.
ti-ina3221-16.relation: control: averaged channel current > warning limit -> Warning pin (inferred -> SOCTHERM OC2 on Orin Nano)
ti-ina3221-16.quote: The warning alert monitors the averaged value of each shunt-voltage channel. ... The device compares the averaged value to the value programmed in the corresponding-channel Warning Alert Limit register to determine if the averaged value has been exceeded, indicating whether the average current is too high.

ti-ina3221-17.claim: In the Linux driver, curr*_max is the warning (average) limit and curr*_crit the critical (instantaneous) limit, each with an alarm flag, which NVIDIA's guide names the rail average and instantaneous current limits.
ti-ina3221-17.relation: control thresholds exposed in sysfs (not exported as telemetry)
ti-ina3221-17.quote: curr[123]_max Warning alert current(mA) setting, activates the corresponding alarm when the respective current average is above this value.

ti-ina3221-18.claim: On earlier Jetson modules NVIDIA explicitly documents that the INA3221 alert outputs feed SOC_THERM, and that asserted alerts make SOC_THERM hardware reduce module power; the Orin r36 guide gives per-limit SOCTHERM_OC pins but no equally explicit wiring sentence for Orin Nano.
ti-ina3221-18.relation: control (feedback note): INA3221 alert -> SOC_THERM -> reduced CPU/GPU clocks/power
ti-ina3221-18.quote: The Jetson module feeds INA3221 outputs into SOC_THERM input. When one or more alert outputs are asserted, the SOC_THERM hardware reduces module power consumption to avoid violating current limits.
ti-ina3221-18.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide : Hardware Setup (L4T 32.4.3)

ti-ina3221-19.claim: The older NVIDIA guide states that the INA3221 warning signal (average current over limit) triggers CPU/GPU hardware throttling through SOCTHERM_OC (pre-Orin modules).
ti-ina3221-19.relation: control (feedback note): VDD_IN average current > warning limit -> CPU/GPU throttling
ti-ina3221-19.quote: ti,current-warning-limit-ma: Channel average current limit in milliamperes. The INA3221 warning signal is asserted when the channel’s average current exceeds this limit, triggering CPU/GPU hardware throttling via Jetson SOCTHEM_OC.
ti-ina3221-19.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Linux Developer Guide : Hardware Setup (L4T 32.4.3)
ti-ina3221-19.section: Voltage and Current Monitor (device tree properties)

ti-ina3221-20.claim: CAUTION: SOCTHERM OC numbering differs between modules (on Xavier NX OC1 = instantaneous power, OC3 = average power, the reverse of the Orin r36 table), so OC-pin meanings must not be carried over between Jetson generations.
ti-ina3221-20.relation: none (documentation caveat on OC pin semantics)
ti-ina3221-20.quote: Xavier NX: OC1: instant power OC2: under voltage OC3: average power
ti-ina3221-20.doc_title: NVIDIA Developer Forums: Jetson OC Alarm Values (reply by WayneWWW, 2023-12-18; staff role not shown in raw export)

ti-ina3221-21.claim: The INA3221 summation function adds single shunt-voltage conversions of selected channels and is only a valid current total when all included channels use the same shunt resistor; it is a sum of channels, not a separate rail.
ti-ina3221-21.relation: summation channel (curr4) = sum of included channel currents (identity, only if equal shunts)
ti-ina3221-21.quote: For the summation limit to have a meaningful value, use the same shunt-resistor value on all included channels. Unless equal shunt-resistor values are used for each channel, do not use this function to add the individual conversion values directly together in the Shunt-Voltage Sum register to report the total current.

ti-ina3221-22.claim: The kernel exposes the summation as curr4_input (sum of channel currents) only when all channels share one shunt value, and NVIDIA's guide calls j=4 the summation channel.
ti-ina3221-22.relation: identity: curr4_input = sum of curr1..3 of non-excluded channels
ti-ina3221-22.quote: curr4_input Sum of current(mA) measurement channels, (only available when all channels use the same resistor value for their shunt resistors)

ti-ina3221-23.claim: AGAINST using the summation channel as module power: in the upstream Orin NX/Nano device tree all three channels (VDD_IN, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV, VDD_SOC) use 5000 uOhm shunts and none is excluded from summation, so curr4 would add the sub-rails to VDD_IN (which already contains them) and double-count; whether NVIDIA's L4T device tree differs was not found.
ti-ina3221-23.relation: against orin_power_watts = V x curr4 (would double-count cpu_gpu_power_watts inside VDD_IN)
ti-ina3221-23.quote: input@0 { reg = <0x0>; label = "VDD_IN"; shunt-resistor-micro-ohms = <5000>; }; input@1 { reg = <0x1>; label = "VDD_CPU_GPU_CV"; shunt-resistor-micro-ohms = <5000>; }; input@2 { reg = <0x2>; label = "VDD_SOC"; shunt-resistor-micro-ohms = <5000>;

ti-ina3221-24.claim: The DT binding lets a channel be excluded from the summation (ti,summation-disable) when shunts differ or a channel should not trigger the Critical pin, so the summation contents are a per-board configuration choice.
ti-ina3221-24.quote: If this is not the case or if a channel should not be used for triggering the critical alert pin, then this property can be used exclude specific channels from the summation control function.

ti-ina3221-25.claim: AGAINST orin_power_watts being the sign's input power on ~56 V signs: an INA3221 input must not exceed 26 V, so it cannot sit on the 56 V supply; the 56 V input power is measured by the INA238 instead, and the INA3221 rails are downstream.
ti-ina3221-25.relation: against identity orin_power_watts = input_power_watts (at least on supply_56v devices); supports orin_power_watts -> input_power_watts (containment)
ti-ina3221-25.quote: This register stores the bus voltage reading, VBUS, for channel 1. Full-scale range = 32.76V (decimal = 7FF8); LSB (BD0) = 8mV. Although the input range is 26V, the full-scale range of the ADC scaling is 32.76V. Do not apply more than 26V.

ti-ina3221-26.claim: The Orin Nano module's VDD_IN accepts at most 20 V (5 V only for legacy MODULE_ID-low modules) and must be supplied by the carrier board, so on 56 V signs (and possibly 12 V signs) a carrier/sign converter sits between the INA238-measured input and the module; module power is then one part of sign input power, alongside converter losses and other loads (display, modem, heater).
ti-ina3221-26.relation: containment: orin_power_watts -> input_power_watts (input_power_watts >= orin_power_watts + other loads + conversion loss); wiring needs BusPas confirmation
ti-ina3221-26.quote: Module ID strap: Indicates whether the module is a legacy type supporting only 5V on VDD_IN (tied to GND on the module) or an advanced type supporting from 5V to 20V on VDD_IN (floating on the module - pulled high on the carrier board).
ti-ina3221-26.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (Connect Tech mirror)
ti-ina3221-26.section: Table 17: Power and System Control Pin Descriptions (pin 217 MODULE_ID); Table 22 Recommended Operating Conditions

ti-ina3221-27.claim: VDD_IN is supplied by the carrier board, and all module interfaces run from on-module rails, so peripherals on the carrier (e.g. modem, display, heater) are outside VDD_IN; their load enters sign input power without passing through orin_power_watts (whether the modem is on the carrier or powered via the module is a BusPas question).
ti-ina3221-27.relation: carrier-board loads (e.g. LTE modem activity) -> input_power_watts directly, not via orin_power_watts (conditional on wiring)
ti-ina3221-27.quote: VDD_IN must be supplied by the carrier board that the Jetson Orin Nano is designed to connect to. All Jetson Orin Nano interfaces are referenced to on-module voltage rails and no I/O voltage is required to be supplied to the module.
ti-ina3221-27.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (Connect Tech mirror)

ti-ina3221-28.claim: NVIDIA's tegrastats reports, per INA3221 rail (VDD_IN, VDD_CPU_GPU_CV, VDD_SOC), the current and average power in milliwatts; a heartbeat service could take cpu_gpu_power_watts (and possibly device_power_watts) from such rail power, which would make them software readings of the same INA3221 as orin_power_watts (inferred, not documented by BusPas).
ti-ina3221-28.relation: possible identity/redundancy (inferred): cpu_gpu_power_watts = VDD_CPU_GPU_CV rail power; device_power_watts may equal a VDD_IN rail power reading (redundant with orin_power_watts)
ti-ina3221-28.quote: VDDX Y /Z ... Power consumption statistics for a power block. | Name of the power rail * | Block’s current power consumption in milliwatts | Block’s average power consumption in milliwatts
ti-ina3221-28.doc_title: Tegrastats Utility — Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4.3

ti-ina3221-29.claim: By default the INA3221 averages 1 sample with a 1.1 ms conversion time, so a register read is a near-instantaneous snapshot; a 120-s-sampled orin_power_watts hourly mean is a mean of snapshots, not an energy integral like input_energy_rate_w (measurement-model difference, not a causal relation).
ti-ina3221-29.relation: none (measurement model: snapshot sampling vs integrated counter; affects residual noise)
ti-ina3221-29.quote: Averaging mode. These bits set the number of samples that are collected and averaged together. 000 = 1 (default) ... 100 = 1.1ms (default)

ti-ina3221-30.claim: INA3221 shunt offset is at most ±80 µV and gain error at most 0.25%; with the 5 mΩ shunts in the upstream Orin Nano device tree this is roughly ±16 mA current offset per channel, a bound for the measurement noise of orin_power_watts.
ti-ina3221-30.relation: none (measurement error bound for residual tolerance)
ti-ina3221-30.quote: High accuracy: – Offset voltage: ±80µV (maximum) – Gain error: 0.25% (maximum)

ti-ina3221-31.claim: The dataset README attributes orin_power_watts to the INA3221 rail monitor and input power to the INA238, but warns that metric meanings are the authors' reading, not vendor documentation, so the channel behind orin_power_watts and the definition of device_power_watts are inferred.
ti-ina3221-31.quote: The endpoint's `# HELP` only repeats the metric name, so **units, meanings and notes are our reading of the names and of the data, not vendor documentation**.

workload-1.claim: On Orin Nano/NX the INA3221 channel VDD_CPU_GPU_CV carries CPU, GPU and CV (DLA/PVA) power; the doc's 'CPU, CPU' is evidently a typo for 'CPU, GPU'. If cpu_gpu_power_watts reads this channel, CPU and GPU workload (DeepStream inference, tracker, software encode) lands there.
workload-1.relation: deepstream_running -> cpu_gpu_power_watts (physical: CPU/GPU load raises rail power); the mapping of cpu_gpu_power_watts to this channel is inferred
workload-1.quote: Channel 2: VDD_CPU_GPU_CV Total power consumed by CPU, CPU and CV cores i.e. DLA and PVA
workload-1.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-1.section: Power Monitor > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series (INA3221 rail names)

workload-2.claim: The VDD_SOC rail powers the memory subsystem and the video engines (NVDEC, NVENC, VI, VIC, ISP). DeepStream decode, VIC scaling/conversion and memory traffic therefore land on VDD_SOC, not on VDD_CPU_GPU_CV.
workload-2.relation: deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts via VDD_SOC (an unobserved rail contained in VDD_IN); this part is NOT in cpu_gpu_power_watts
workload-2.quote: Channel 3: VDD_SOC Power consumed by SOC core which supplies to memory subsystem and various engines like nvdec, nvenc, vi, vic, isp etc.
workload-2.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-2.section: Power Monitor > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

workload-3.claim: INA3221 channel 1 (VDD_IN) is total module power. If orin_power_watts reads VDD_IN, it contains both VDD_CPU_GPU_CV and VDD_SOC.
workload-3.relation: cpu_gpu_power_watts is contained in orin_power_watts (containment), valid only if orin_power_watts = VDD_IN and cpu_gpu_power_watts = VDD_CPU_GPU_CV
workload-3.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-3.section: Power Monitor > Jetson Orin NX Series and Jetson Orin Nano Series

workload-4.claim: The Orin Nano module's power monitor measures only module rails, and VDD_IN is supplied by the carrier board. Carrier-board loads (LTE modem, Wi-Fi card, display, heater, camera) are therefore outside every INA3221 channel and appear only at the sign's input monitor.
workload-4.relation: orin_power_watts is contained in input_power_watts (containment); modem/Wi-Fi power is in input_power_watts but not in orin_power_watts
workload-4.quote: VDD_IN must be supplied by the carrier board that the Jetson Orin Nano is designed to connect to. ... Jetson Orin Nano has a single three-channel INA that can measure power of CPU_GPU_CV combined rail, Core, and module input power.
workload-4.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)

workload-5.claim: Orin Nano has no DLA (and the nvpmodel tables list 0 PVA cores), so DeepStream inference on Orin Nano runs on the GPU. The 'CV' part of VDD_CPU_GPU_CV is effectively absent, so the rail is about CPU + GPU.
workload-5.relation: deepstream_running (nvinfer) -> cpu_gpu_power_watts; no DLA/PVA path on Orin Nano
workload-5.quote: enable-dla Indicates whether to use the DLA engine for inferencing. Note: DLA is supported only on NVIDIA® Jetson AGX Orin™ and NVIDIA® Jetson Orin NX™.

workload-6.claim: The nvpmodel tables for Orin Nano 4GB list 0 DLA cores and 0 PVA cores in every power mode, and 'nvenc: n/a'.
workload-6.relation: CV share of VDD_CPU_GPU_CV is zero on Orin Nano
workload-6.quote: DLA cores 0 0 0 ... PVA cores 0 0 0 ... dce: 384 nvenc: n/a se: 307.2
workload-6.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-6.section: Supported Modes and Power Efficiency > NVP Model Clock Configuration for Jetson Orin Nano 4GB

workload-7.claim: DeepStream offloads its compute to several hardware engines (VIC, GPU, DLA, NVDEC, NVENC), so its power spreads over more than one rail.
workload-7.relation: deepstream_running -> cpu_gpu_power_watts (GPU) and -> orin_power_watts (GPU + VDD_SOC engines)
workload-7.quote: The core SDK consists of several hardware accelerator plugins that use accelerators such as VIC, GPU, DLA, NVDEC and NVENC. By performing all the compute heavy operations in a dedicated accelerator, DeepStream can achieve highest performance for video analytic applications.
workload-7.doc_title: NVIDIA DeepStream SDK Developer Guide - Overview

workload-8.claim: The DeepStream hardware decoder uses the NVDEC engine, which sits on VDD_SOC.
workload-8.relation: deepstream_running (decode) -> orin_power_watts via VDD_SOC (not via cpu_gpu_power_watts)
workload-8.quote: The plugin accepts an encoded bitstream and uses the NVDEC hardware engine to decode the bitstream.

workload-9.claim: NVDEC uses dynamic frequency scaling, so decoder power depends on the decode load (streams, resolution, frame rate), not just on whether the process runs.
workload-9.relation: deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts is load-dependent (DVFS); a process-running fraction is only a proxy
workload-9.quote: For low-power operations, the video decoder can operate at the lowest possible frequency while maintaining real-time decoding using dynamic frequency scaling techniques.
workload-9.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)

workload-10.claim: On Jetson, nvvideoconvert does colour conversion and scaling on VIC by default (VDD_SOC), not on the GPU.
workload-10.relation: deepstream_running (convert/scale) -> orin_power_watts via VDD_SOC by default; to cpu_gpu_power_watts only if compute-hw=GPU
workload-10.quote: compute-hw Type of computing hardware: 0: Default (GPU for gDPU, VIC for Jetson) 1: GPU 2: VIC

workload-11.claim: nvinfer runs inference with TensorRT on the GPU, and by default scales input frames to network resolution on VIC on Jetson. Inference load goes to VDD_CPU_GPU_CV; pre-scaling goes to VDD_SOC.
workload-11.relation: deepstream_running -> cpu_gpu_power_watts (TensorRT GPU inference); deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts (VIC scaling via VDD_SOC)
workload-11.quote: The Gst-nvinfer plugin does inferencing on input data using NVIDIA ® TensorRT™. ... scaling-compute-hw Compute hardware to use for scaling frames / object crops to network resolution (ignored if input-tensor-meta enabled) Integer 0: Platform default – GPU (dGPU), VIC (Jetson)

workload-12.claim: Orin Nano has no NVENC hardware encoder, so any video encoding in the sign's pipeline must run in software on the CPU. That load lands on VDD_CPU_GPU_CV.
workload-12.quote: The NVIDIA® Jetson™ Orin Nano does not have the NVENC engine. This application note provides information about how to migrate to software encoding using the libav (FFmpeg) encoders
workload-12.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Software Encode in Orin Nano

workload-13.claim: The Orin Nano data sheet confirms that video encoding is done on the CPU cores in software.
workload-13.quote: Video Encode: • 1080p30 Supported via CPU Cores with Software
workload-13.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)

workload-14.claim: The DeepStream multi-object tracker runs on CPU and GPU (PVA only on Jetsons that have it, which Orin Nano does not), so tracker load lands on VDD_CPU_GPU_CV.
workload-14.quote: It supports multi-stream, multi-object tracking in the batch processing mode for efficient processing on CPU and GPU (and PVA for Jetson).

workload-15.claim: The on-screen-display plugin draws on the GPU by default (CPU mode optional), so overlay drawing also lands on VDD_CPU_GPU_CV.
workload-15.quote: process-mode Indicates the mode used to draw the objects Default mode: GPU mode 0: CPU mode 1: GPU mode

workload-16.claim: CPU frequency follows CPU load (cpufreq), and GPU 3D frequency scaling is on by default. Higher DeepStream utilisation therefore raises clocks and voltages, and with them CPU/GPU power: a control mechanism.
workload-16.quote: cpufreq implements load-based scaling , which adjusts the CPU frequency according to how busy the CPU is. CPU thermal management, however, can override the target frequency of cpufreq . ... GPU 3D frequency scaling is enabled by default.
workload-16.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-16.section: Power and performance knobs; GPU 3D Frequency Scaling

workload-17.claim: The DeepStream quick start tells users to pin clocks at maximum (nvpmodel plus jetson_clocks; MAXN SUPER on Orin Nano). If BusPas did this, DVFS is disabled and the power-versus-load relation changes: a higher idle floor and a smaller load slope.
workload-17.relation: deepstream_running -> cpu_gpu_power_watts slope depends on clock configuration (unknown)
workload-17.quote: After you have installed DeepStream SDK, run these commands on the Jetson device to boost the clocks: $ sudo nvpmodel -m 0 $ sudo jetson_clocks For Jetson Orin Nano modules, use sudo nvpmodel -m 2 instead of -m 0 to enable MAXN SUPER mode.

workload-18.claim: Memory (EMC) frequency follows measured memory bandwidth usage, not the amount of memory allocated. DeepStream memory traffic raises EMC clocks (VDD_SOC 'memory subsystem'); allocated-but-idle RAM does not.
workload-18.relation: deepstream_running -> orin_power_watts (control: bandwidth-driven EMC DFS); argues AGAINST mem_used_gb -> power
workload-18.quote: If current memory bandwidth usage exceeds 30%, the BPMP will scale up the EMC frequency, and if the memory bandwidth usage is lower than 20%, the BPMP will scale down the EMC frequency.
workload-18.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance

workload-19.claim: When module power (VDD_IN) exceeds the TDP limit, hardware throttles CPU and GPU clocks; for Orin Nano 4GB the limit is 10 W average. This is a same-hour feedback (CPU/GPU power -> module power -> throttle -> CPU/GPU power), so record it as a feedback note, not an edge.
workload-19.relation: feedback note: orin_power_watts over limit throttles cpu_gpu_power_watts (control, lag-0 cycle)
workload-19.quote: When the module power consumption exceeds the configured power limit, the module will perform hardware-based clock throttling on the GPU and CPU for a configurable period.
workload-19.doc_title: Jetson Linux Developer Guide r36.4 - Platform Power and Performance
workload-19.section: Power Monitor > Jetson Orin NX/Nano (TDP average and instantaneous power limits)

workload-20.claim: DeepStream's nvmsgbroker plugin can send analytics messages to a server (Kafka, MQTT, AMQP, Azure, Redis). If BusPas uses it over LTE, DeepStream activity would add WWAN uplink traffic. Both nodes are context roots, so this is a confounder note, not an edge.
workload-20.relation: deepstream_running ~ wwan_tx_rate (possible shared driver; context-context, no edge)
workload-20.quote: This plugin sends payload messages to the server using a specified communication protocol.

workload-21.claim: LTE modem power during a data connection depends on the network settings and the data transfer rate.
workload-21.relation: wwan_tx_rate, wwan_rx_rate -> input_power_watts (physical: modem power, unobserved, is part of input power)
workload-21.quote: Talk/Data Network connection is ongoing. In this mode, the power consumption is decided by network setting and data transfer rate.

workload-22.claim: An LTE Cat-4 modem draws about 18-29 mA idle (registered, USB connected or not) and about 600-750 mA during LTE-FDD data transfer at 22.3 dBm, at VBAT 3.8 V typical. That is roughly 0.1 W versus 2.3-2.8 W, a large share of a sign drawing about 10 W.

workload-22.quote: LTE-FDD @ PF=64 (USB connected) 29 mA ... LTE-FDD B1 @ 22.3 dBm 743 mA ... LTE-FDD B12 @ 22.3 dBm 600 mA

workload-23.section: 3.6.2 Decrease Voltage Drop; 3.6.3 Reference Design for Power Supply

workload-24.claim: M.2-form-factor Quectel LTE modems run from the host connector's 3.3 V supply, again a carrier-board rail.
workload-24.relation: M.2 modem power is in input_power_watts, not in orin_power_watts

workload-24.doc_title: Quectel EM05 Series LTE Standard Specification V1.7

workload-25.claim: LTE modem supply current in connected mode rises with RF transmit power: about 270 mA at 0 dBm to 650 mA at maximum. Transmit power is not observed.
workload-25.relation: modem power depends on transmit power (unobserved) as well as traffic; wwan_tx_rate -> input_power_watts is noisy

workload-25.doc_title: u-blox LARA-R6 series Data sheet (UBX-21004391) R10

workload-26.claim: LTE uplink transmit power is set by the standard's power-control formula. It grows with the allocated uplink bandwidth (resource blocks, which scale with uplink data rate) and with downlink path loss (radio conditions, not observed), and is capped at PCMAX.
workload-26.relation: wwan_tx_rate -> modem TX power (unobserved) -> input_power_watts; path loss is an unobserved site-specific modifier
workload-26.quote: 10 log10 ( M PUSCH,c (i )) + PO_PUSCH,c ( j ) + α c ( j ) ⋅ PLc + Δ TF, c (i ) + f c (i ) ... PLc is the downlink path loss estimate calculated in the UE for serving cell c in dB

workload-27.claim: Measured LTE device power is linear in throughput while connected: P = au*tu + ad*td + b, with au = 438 mW/Mbps uplink and ad = 52 mW/Mbps downlink. Uplink bytes cost about 8.4 times more power than downlink bytes. (Smartphone measurement, 2012 network.)
workload-27.relation: input_power_watts increases with ~8x more weight on wwan_tx_rate than on wwan_rx_rate (physical)
workload-27.quote: Assume uplink throughput is tu (Mbps) and downlink throughput is td (Mbps), the power level (mW) for uplink is Pu = αu tu + β and for downlink Pd = αd td + β. ... LTE 438.39 51.97 1288.04 8.44
workload-27.doc_title: Junxian Huang, Performance and Power Characterization of Cellular Networks and Mobile Application Optimizations (PhD thesis, 2013)
workload-27.section: 6.3.2 Power Model for Data Transfer, Table 6.2

workload-28.claim: After each LTE transfer the radio stays in a high-power tail (about 11.6 s at about 1 W), so energy per hour depends on how many separate bursts occur, not only on bytes. This argues that the hourly-bytes-to-power relation is nonlinear or weak for sparse traffic.
workload-28.relation: evidence AGAINST a simple linear bytes/hour -> power edge; burst count (unobserved) matters
workload-28.quote: LTE appears to have longest tail (11.576 seconds) with highest tail base power (1060.04 mW). ... if only one packet is transferred, the energy usage considering both promotion and tail energy for LTE, 3G and WiFi is 12.76J, 7.38J and 0.04J
workload-28.doc_title: Junxian Huang, Performance and Power Characterization of Cellular Networks and Mobile Application Optimizations (PhD thesis, 2013)
workload-28.section: 6.3.1 Power model for RRC and DRX

In 2.4/5 GHz transmit its supply draw averages about 369-722 and in receive about 234-348 (units not printed; mA at 3.3 V is implied, i.e. about 0.8-2.4 W).
workload-29.relation: wifi_hotspot_running -> input_power_watts (physical: radio power on a carrier rail)

workload-30.relation: Wi-Fi power is in input_power_watts, not in orin_power_watts (if BusPas uses a carrier M.2 Wi-Fi card)

workload-31.claim: The NVIDIA Orin Nano dev kit carries its Wi-Fi card in the carrier board's M.2 Key-E slot, not on the module.
workload-31.relation: Wi-Fi radio is a carrier-board load (not in orin_power_watts)
workload-31.quote: 12 M.2 slot (Key-E, Type 2230) Populated with the included wireless module

workload-32.claim: In SoftAP (hotspot) mode the Wi-Fi interface never sleeps, even with no traffic. Measured phone power rose from about 20-30 mW (tethering off) to about 270-333 mW (tethering on, idle): a roughly constant additive cost while the hotspot is active.
workload-32.relation: wifi_hotspot_running -> input_power_watts (physical: ~+0.25-0.3 W baseline, more with traffic)
workload-32.quote: When operating in the SoftAP mode, the Wi-Fi interface of a smartphone is always put in the high power state and never sleeps even when there is no data traffic going on.
workload-32.doc_title: Han et al., DozyAP: Power-Efficient Wi-Fi Tethering (MobiSys 2012)

workload-33.claim: IEEE 802.11 power saving is designed for stations; the AP buffers frames for sleeping stations, which implies the AP itself stays awake. A hotspot therefore keeps its radio powered.
workload-33.relation: supports wifi_hotspot_running -> input_power_watts as a step change
workload-33.quote: IEEE-802.11 was designed with power saving in mind for stations. ... To assist stations with power saving, Access Points (APs) are designed to buffer frames for a station when that station is in power save mode
workload-33.doc_title: Linux Wireless documentation - Power Savings on IEEE-802.11

workload-34.claim: wifi_hotspot_running records whether a systemd service is active, not the radio state or connected clients. Its meaning is inferred by the dataset authors.
workload-34.quote: 1 when the Wi-Fi hotspot service is active (checked with systemd), 0 otherwise. Usually 0. *Source: `cmd:systemctl`.*

workload-35.claim: WWAN rx/tx are byte totals logged by the heartbeat service that restart about daily. Hourly increases give bytes per hour, i.e. mean throughput, which hides burst structure.
workload-35.quote: `device_wwan_rx_gb` | gauge, GB | Data received over the cellular (WWAN) modem. *Source: `sqlite:heartbeat`.* **Note:** Typed as a gauge, but behaves like a running total that restarts about once a day

workload-36.claim: MemTotal minus MemFree counts the page cache and tmpfs/shmem as 'used'. mem_used_gb therefore also tracks file caching, not only application allocations.
workload-36.relation: definition only; no power relation implied
workload-36.quote: MemFree Total free RAM. On highmem systems, the sum of LowFree+HighFree ... Cached In-memory cache for files read from the disk (the pagecache) as well as tmpfs & shmem.

workload-37.claim: DRAM supply current depends mainly on access activity: burst read about 285 mA and burst write about 217 mA on VDD2, versus active standby about 26 mA and precharge standby about 20 mA. How much memory is allocated does not enter. (LPDDR4 part; Orin Nano uses LPDDR5, so this is an analogue.)
workload-37.relation: AGAINST mem_used_gb -> power: DRAM power follows bandwidth/activity, not allocation
workload-37.doc_title: Micron 200b Automotive LPDDR4/LPDDR4X SDRAM data sheet

workload-38.claim: DRAM refresh is issued to every bank at a fixed interval whatever the contents, so refresh power does not depend on how much memory is in use.
workload-38.quote: An all-bank REFRESH command (REFab) issues a REFRESH command to every bank in a channel. ... In general, a REFRESH command needs to be issued to the device regularly every tREFI interval.
workload-38.doc_title: Micron 200b Automotive LPDDR4/LPDDR4X SDRAM data sheet

workload-39.claim: The only documented DRAM mechanism by which unused memory could save power is partial-array self-refresh (PASR) bank masking. It needs OS support and acts only in self-refresh; nothing found says Jetson Linux uses it.
workload-39.relation: AGAINST mem_used_gb -> power during operation (PASR at most, unconfirmed)
workload-39.quote: When a mask bit is asserted (OP[n] = 1), refresh to that bank is disabled.
workload-39.doc_title: Micron 200b Automotive LPDDR4/LPDDR4X SDRAM data sheet
workload-39.section: Mode Registers, Table 58 (MR16 PASR Bank Mask) notes

workload-40.quote: Support for low-power modes: o Software controllable entry/exit from self-refresh, power down, and deep power down o Hardware dynamic entry/exit from power down, self-refresh o Pads use DPD mode during idle periods
workload-40.doc_title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Series Data Sheet DS-11105-001 v0.1 (preliminary)

workload-41.claim: deepstream_running only records that the process exists (pgrep), not pipeline load. The README notes the app is usually not running.
workload-41.relation: definition only; weakens deepstream_running as a load proxy
workload-41.quote: 1 when the DeepStream video-analytics application process is running. *Source: `proc:pgrep`.* **Note:** The median is 0: on most devices the application is usually not running.

workload-42.claim: ds_error_rate counts 'consumer errors' found in the DeepStream log. Its meaning is undocumented and no source links it to power.
workload-42.quote: Number of DeepStream consumer errors found in the DeepStream log. *Source: `log:deepstream`.* **Note:** Falls back to 0 about once a day

workload-43.claim: cpu_gpu_power_watts and orin_power_watts come from different services (heartbeat sqlite vs sysfs INA3221). Neither the channel nor the computation is documented, so the containment edge is inferred.
workload-43.quote: `device_cpu_gpu_power_watts` | gauge, W | CPU + GPU power draw, as logged by the heartbeat service. ... `device_orin_power_watts` | gauge, W | Power drawn by the Jetson Orin compute module (rail monitor). *Source: `sysfs:ina3221`.*

solar-1.claim: Controller family: the SRNE Modbus map (used by Renogy Rover, an SRNE OEM) has the same register set as the sqlite:mppt fields. These are battery SOC, battery voltage, charging current to the battery, controller and battery temperature, load DC voltage, current and power, solar panel voltage and current, charging power, and load on/off. The SRNE family is the best match; EPEVER is second.
solar-1.quote: 0100H 2 R Battery capacity SOC 0 to 100 Current battery capacity value % 0101H 2 R Battery voltage Battery voltage * 0.1 V Charging current (to battery) 0102H 2 R Charging current * 0.01 A Controller temperature ... Battery temperature 0104H 2 R Street light (load) voltage
solar-1.section: PDU address table, Dynamic controller information (whitespace normalised from table)

solar-2.claim: SRNE's own display menu uses the dataset's wording: 'Remaining battery capacity' for SOC, 'Controller temperature', 'Charging power' and 'Discharging power' for load power. This supports the SRNE-family identification.
solar-2.quote: LoadState： OFF Load in "ON" or "OFF" state LoadCrt : 0A Load current BatSoc： 100% Remaining battery capacity DevTemp： 27 ℃ Controller temperature ChagPower： 0W Charging power LoadPower： 0W Discharging power
solar-2.doc_title: SRNE ML4860 Solar Charge and Discharge Controller User Manual

solar-3.claim: In the SRNE protocol, load power (0106H) equals load voltage x load current. The worked example is off by a factor of 10 (0078H=12.0 V x 00C8H=2.00 A is reported as 240 W), so the identity is defined but the example arithmetic is wrong.
solar-3.quote: 00F0H is the load power (decimal 240W) which can also be calculated via formula: load voltage * load current
solar-3.section: 4.8 To read load voltage, current and power

solar-4.claim: In the SRNE/Rover protocol, 'Charging power' (0109H) is the solar-panel (input-side) power, solar panel voltage x solar panel current, not battery voltage x battery charge current. This argues against the README's reading of mppt_charge_power as power delivered into the battery.
solar-4.quote: 00D8H is solar panel charging power (decimal 216 W) which can also be calculated via formula: solar panel voltage * solar panel charging current
solar-4.section: 3.9 To read solar panel voltage, charging current and charging power (same text in SRNE MODBUS PROTOCOL V3.9 section 4.9)

solar-5.claim: The README reads mppt_charge_power as battery-side power (charge controller to battery). This is the dataset authors' inference, not vendor documentation, and it conflicts with the SRNE definition above.
solar-5.relation: mppt_charge_power = mppt_battery_voltage x mppt_battery_charge_current (README reading, inferred; disputed)
solar-5.quote: Power the charge controller delivers into the battery (0 at night). *Source: `sqlite:mppt`.*
solar-5.section: Battery and solar charge controller (MPPT), device_mppt_charge_power

solar-6.claim: The protocol defines two different currents: solar panel current flows into the controller (input), and charging current flows from the controller to the battery (output). mppt_solar_current and mppt_battery_charge_current are therefore the input and output of the DC/DC converter, not two sensors of the same quantity.
solar-6.relation: none (distinct input/output currents; linked only via conversion, see energy-balance fact)
solar-6.quote: 0102H 2 R A Charging current (to battery) Charging current * 0.01 ... 0108H 2 R A Solar panel current (to controller) Solar panel current * 0.01 The solar panel current is 2.66A

solar-7.claim: MPPT energy conservation: battery-side power equals PV-side power times the conversion efficiency. Because V_mpp is above V_bat, the battery charge current exceeds the PV current. So the battery charge current is fixed by PV power, battery voltage and efficiency.
solar-7.relation: mppt_battery_voltage x mppt_battery_charge_current = eta x mppt_solar_voltage x mppt_solar_current (physical, eta<1)
solar-7.quote: Normally, the VMpp is always higher than VBat. Due to the principle of energy conservation, the IBat is always higher than IPV. The greater the difference between VMpp &VBat, the greater the difference between IPV& IBat.

solar-8.claim: Conversion efficiency is high but below 100% (max 98% DC/DC). The missing power (P_in - P_out) is conversion loss.
solar-8.relation: P_out = eta x P_in with eta <= 0.98

solar-9.claim: Buck converter efficiency is output power over output power plus total losses. The losses are switching, inductor, capacitor and other losses, and they grow with throughput.
solar-9.quote: Figure 2 shows the power losses of synchronous buck converter, including the switching losses, the inductor losses, the capacitor losses and other losses. The efficiency calculation is shown in Equation 1 and Equation 2.
solar-9.doc_title: TI SLVAEQ9 An Accurate Approach for Calculating the Efficiency of a Synchronous Buck Converter
solar-9.section: 2 Power Losses Calculation for Synchronous Buck Converter

solar-10.claim: In a power converter, dissipated internal power raises the device temperature above ambient: T ≈ T_ambient + R_theta x power loss. Conversion losses (rising with charge power) and the ambient temperature both heat the controller. enclosure_temperature is a valid ambient only if the controller sits in that enclosure (unconfirmed).
solar-10.quote: As with any power conversion device, the LMR3650x dissipates internal power while operating. The effect of this power dissipation is to raise the internal temperature of the converter above ambient. The internal die temperature (TJ) is a function of the ambient temperature, the power loss

solar-11.claim: The charge controller's own documentation says its heat sink heats up in operation (passive heat-sink cooling). This supports self-heating of the controller-temperature sensor.
solar-11.quote: Install the controller in a well-ventilated place; the controller's heat sink may become hot during operation.

solar-12.claim: Derating control: on SRNE controllers, above a set temperature the charging current falls in linear proportion to temperature and discharging stops. With the heating fact this forms a lag-0 cycle (charge power -> controller temp -> charge current), so write it as a feedback note, not an edge.
solar-12.relation: feedback note: mppt_controller_temperature limits mppt_battery_charge_current / mppt_charge_power and can switch load off
solar-12.quote: The controller employs a built-in over-temperature protection mechanism. When temperature surpasses the set value, the charging current will decline in linear proportion to the temperature and discharging will be halted so as to curb the temperature rise of the controller
solar-12.doc_title: SRNE ML4860 Solar Charge and Discharge Controller User Manual

solar-13.claim: On the Renogy Rover, 'controller temperature' is the heat-sink temperature. Charge-current derating starts above 65 °C and the controller shuts down above 85 °C, so derating acts only at high heat-sink temperatures.
solar-13.relation: feedback note: mppt_controller_temperature > 65 C -> reduced mppt_battery_charge_current
solar-13.quote: If the temperature of the controller heat sink exceeds 65℃, the controller will automatically start reducing the charging current. The controller will shut down when the temperature exceeds 85℃.

solar-14.claim: EPEVER thresholds, for comparison: charging-power reduction starts at 81 °C internal temperature and charging stops above 85 °C. The exact thresholds depend on the model.
solar-14.relation: feedback note: mppt_controller_temperature >= 81 C -> reduced mppt_charge_power
solar-14.quote: When the controller's internal temperature reaches 81℃, the charging power automatic reduction function is enabled. Temperature increases by 1 ℃, and the charging power is reduced by 5%, 10%, 20%, and 40%. If the internal temperature exceeds 85℃, the controller stops charging the battery.

solar-15.claim: The load output is a switched copy of the battery bus with a small series drop: load voltage ≈ battery voltage minus at most 0.23 V when the load is on. Load current through this path also dissipates a small amount of power (≤0.23 V x I_load) in the controller; that is an inference.
solar-15.relation: mppt_battery_voltage -> mppt_load_voltage (mppt_load_voltage ≈ mppt_battery_voltage - ≤0.23 V, when mppt_load_state=1)

solar-16.claim: Renogy (SRNE OEM) states that the load terminal is powered from the battery, not regulated, so the load voltage follows the battery voltage.
solar-16.relation: mppt_battery_voltage -> mppt_load_voltage (identity up to switch drop)
solar-16.quote: The DC load is powered by batteries, so ensure that the DC load is compatible with the battery voltage. If a 12V DC load is installed in a 24V battery system, the incorrect connection will damage the charge controller and void the warranty.
solar-16.doc_title: Renogy Rover Li Series MPPT Solar Charge Controller User Manual

solar-17.claim: The load output is switched by a load on/off command register. When load_state is 0, load voltage, current and power should be about 0. With the gating, load_state is a valid context parent of the load nodes.
solar-17.quote: To turn on the load, and knowing the PDU address is 010AH, you need write on/ off command into this address (0001 to turn on the load, 0000 to turn off the load)

solar-18.claim: Against treating load_state as exogenous: the controller turns the load off by itself at low battery voltage (low-voltage disconnect). load_state is then a function of battery voltage, which a context root cannot express; record this as a note.
solar-18.relation: note: mppt_battery_voltage < LVD -> mppt_load_state = 0 (control; load_state is a context root, so not an edge)
solar-18.quote: The battery discharging is automatically stopped when the battery voltage is lower than the low voltage disconnect voltage.

solar-19.claim: Against an exogenous load_state, continued: in the light-control load modes the controller switches the load by PV voltage (on at dusk, off at dawn). Only in manual or 'normal on' mode is the load independent of the sun. The configured mode is a question for BusPas.
solar-19.relation: note: mppt_solar_voltage below light-control threshold -> mppt_load_state=1 (light-control mode only)
solar-19.quote: The solar panel voltage is lower than the light control on voltage, and after a preset time delay , the controller will switch on the load; The solar panel voltage is higher than the light control off voltage, and after a preset time delay , the controller will switch off the load.
solar-19.doc_title: SRNE ML4860 Solar Charge and Discharge Controller User Manual
solar-19.section: Load working modes - Sole light control mode

solar-20.claim: Charge-stage control: once the battery reaches the constant-voltage set point, MPPT stops and the charge current falls. So in absorption and float, charge current and power fall below what the sun could provide. Battery charging also raises battery voltage, which closes a lag-0 loop, so keep battery_voltage -> charge_current as an edge and put the reverse in a feedback note.
solar-20.relation: mppt_battery_voltage -> mppt_battery_charge_current (control); feedback note: charge current raises battery voltage
solar-20.quote: When the battery reaches the constant voltage set point, the charge controller will start to operate in constant charging mode, where it is no longer MPPT charging. The current will drop gradually.
solar-20.doc_title: Renogy Rover Li Series MPPT Solar Charge Controller User Manual
solar-20.section: Charging and Activation Logic - Four Charging Stages (Constant Charging)

solar-21.claim: In float, the loads take almost all the solar power. When the battery is full, charging power is limited by load demand, so load power drives the solar/charge power, the opposite of the daytime direction. Load and battery charging share one battery bus.
solar-21.relation: mppt_load_power -> mppt_charge_power when battery in float (demand-limited, control)
solar-21.quote: At this stage, the loads can access almost all the solar power. If the loads consume more power than the solar panel could provide, the controller will not be able to keep the battery voltage at the floating charging stage.
solar-21.doc_title: SRNE ML4860 Solar Charge and Discharge Controller User Manual

solar-22.claim: The load draws from the battery while the controller supplies the charge current. The net battery current (charge minus load, unobserved) is what moves battery voltage and SOC.
solar-22.relation: net battery current (unobserved) = mppt_battery_charge_current - mppt_load_current; drives mppt_battery_voltage
